metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
units.rightText: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

units.leftText: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
units.rightText: Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.

units.leftText: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
units.rightText: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
rightNotes: 1:3 Cited in 2 Corinthians 4:6|2CO 4:6*

units.leftText: God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness.
units.rightText: And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.

units.leftText: God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.
units.rightText: God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.”

units.leftText: God said, “Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.”
units.rightText: And God said, “Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters.”
rightNotes: 1:6 Or a canopy or a firmament or a vault; also in verses 7, 8, 14, 15, 17, and 20

units.leftText: God made the expanse, and divided the waters which were under the expanse from the waters which were above the expanse; and it was so.
units.rightText: So God made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above. And it was so.

units.leftText: God called the expanse “sky”. There was evening and there was morning, a second day.
units.rightText: God called the expanse “sky.”

units.leftText: God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered together to one place, and let the dry land appear;” and it was so.
units.rightText: And God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” And it was so.

units.leftText: God called the dry land “earth”, and the gathering together of the waters he called “seas”. God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of waters He called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: God said, “Let the earth yield grass, herbs yielding seeds, and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, with their seeds in it, on the earth;” and it was so.
units.rightText: Then God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.” And it was so.

units.leftText: The earth yielded grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, with their seeds in it, after their kind; and God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: There was evening and there was morning, a third day.
units.rightText: And there was evening, and there was morning — the third day.

units.leftText: God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years;
units.rightText: And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.

units.leftText: and let them be for lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth;” and it was so.
units.rightText: And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.

units.leftText: God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.
units.rightText: God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as well.

units.leftText: God set them in the expanse of the sky to give light to the earth,
units.rightText: God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,

units.leftText: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: There was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.
units.rightText: And there was evening, and there was morning — the fourth day.

units.leftText: God said, “Let the waters abound with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”
units.rightText: And God said, “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”

units.leftText: God created the large sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind. God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: God blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”
units.rightText: Then God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”

units.leftText: There was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.
units.rightText: And there was evening, and there was morning — the fifth day.

units.leftText: God said, “Let the earth produce living creatures after their kind, livestock, creeping things, and animals of the earth after their kind;” and it was so.
units.rightText: And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.

units.leftText: God made the animals of the earth after their kind, and the livestock after their kind, and everything that creeps on the ground after its kind. God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crawls upon the earth according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness. Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”
units.rightText: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.”
rightNotes: 1:26 MT; Syriac and over all the beasts of the earth

units.leftText: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
units.rightText: So God created man in His own image;

units.leftText: God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
units.rightText: God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”

units.leftText: God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.
units.rightText: Then God said, “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.
leftNotes: 1:29 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: To every animal of the earth, and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in which there is life, I have given every green herb for food;” and it was so.
units.rightText: And to every beast of the earth and every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth — everything that has the breath of life in it — I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.

units.leftText: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.
units.rightText: And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good.

units.leftText: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished.
units.rightText: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.

units.leftText: On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
units.rightText: And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.
rightNotes: 2:2 Cited in Hebrews 4:4|HEB 4:4*

units.leftText: God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.
units.rightText: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.

units.leftText: This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.
units.rightText: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made them.
leftNotes: 2:4 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).
rightNotes: 2:4 LORD or GOD, with capital letters, represents the proper name of the God of Israel and the one true God, transliterated from the Hebrew as YHWH; here and throughout the Scriptures.

units.leftText: No plant of the field was yet on the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth. There was not a man to till the ground,
units.rightText: Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted, for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.

units.leftText: but a mist went up from the earth, and watered the whole surface of the ground.
units.rightText: But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
rightNotes: 2:6 Or mist

units.leftText: The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
units.rightText: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
rightNotes: 2:7 Or a living soul; cited in 1 Corinthians 15:45|1CO 15:45*

units.leftText: The LORD God planted a garden eastward, in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed.
units.rightText: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.

units.leftText: Out of the ground the LORD God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
units.rightText: Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

units.leftText: A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
units.rightText: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:

units.leftText: The name of the first is Pishon: it flows through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;
units.rightText: The name of the first river is the Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.

units.leftText: and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and onyx stone are also there.
units.rightText: And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.

units.leftText: The name of the second river is Gihon. It is the same river that flows through the whole land of Cush.
units.rightText: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.

units.leftText: The name of the third river is Hiddekel. This is the one which flows in front of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
units.rightText: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Assyria.

units.leftText: The LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
units.rightText: Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

units.leftText: The LORD God commanded the man, saying, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;
units.rightText: And the LORD God commanded him, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,

units.leftText: but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
units.rightText: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”

units.leftText: The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to him.”
units.rightText: The LORD God also said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”
leftNotes: 2:18 or, suitable for, or appropriate for.

units.leftText: Out of the ground the LORD God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called every living creature became its name.
units.rightText: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.

units.leftText: The man gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for man there was not found a helper comparable to him.
units.rightText: The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.
rightNotes: 2:20 Or the man, as in verses 19 and 21

units.leftText: The LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As the man slept, he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
units.rightText: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area with flesh.
rightNotes: 2:21 Or took part of the man’s side; similarly in verse 22

units.leftText: The LORD God made a woman from the rib which he had taken from the man, and brought her to the man.
units.rightText: And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.

units.leftText: The man said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She will be called ‘woman,’ because she was taken out of Man.”
units.rightText: And the man said:

units.leftText: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.
units.rightText: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.
rightNotes: 2:24 LXX and the two will become one flesh; cited in Matthew 19:5|MAT 19:5*, Mark 10:7–8, 1 Corinthians 6:16, and Ephesians 5:31

units.leftText: The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
units.rightText: And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.

units.leftText: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”
units.rightText: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’”
rightNotes: 3:1 Hebrew nachash, translated in this chapter as serpent, is translated in most cases as snake.

units.leftText: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,
units.rightText: The woman answered the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden,

units.leftText: but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’”
units.rightText: but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’”

units.leftText: The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,
units.rightText: “You will not surely die,” the serpent told the woman.

units.leftText: for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
units.rightText: “For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

units.leftText: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.
units.rightText: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom, she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.

units.leftText: Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.
units.rightText: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.

units.leftText: They heard the LORD God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
units.rightText: Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
rightNotes: 3:8 Or at the breezy (time); Hebrew unto the Ruach

units.leftText: The LORD God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”
units.rightText: But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”

units.leftText: The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
units.rightText: “I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.”

units.leftText: God said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”
units.rightText: “Who told you that you were naked?” asked the LORD God. “Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?”

units.leftText: The man said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
units.rightText: And the man answered, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”

units.leftText: The LORD God said to the woman, “What have you done?”
units.rightText: Then the LORD God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?”

units.leftText: The LORD God said to the serpent,
units.rightText: So the LORD God said to the serpent:

units.leftText: I will put hostility between you and the woman,
units.rightText: And I will put enmity between you and the woman,

units.leftText: To the woman he said,
units.rightText: To the woman He said:

units.leftText: To Adam he said,
units.rightText: And to Adam He said:

units.leftText: It will yield thorns and thistles to you;
units.rightText: Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you,

units.leftText: You will eat bread by the sweat of your face until you return to the ground,
units.rightText: By the sweat of your brow

units.leftText: The man called his wife Eve because she would be the mother of all the living.
units.rightText: And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.
rightNotes: 3:20 Eve sounds like the Hebrew for giving life or living.

units.leftText: The LORD God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.
units.rightText: And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.

units.leftText: The LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—”
units.rightText: Then the LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...”

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.
units.rightText: Therefore the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.

units.leftText: So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.
units.rightText: So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.
leftNotes: 3:24 cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10.

units.leftText: The man knew Eve his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Cain, and said, “I have gotten a man with the LORD’s help.”
units.rightText: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain.
leftNotes: 4:1 or, lay with, or, had relations with
rightNotes: 4:1 Cain sounds like the Hebrew for acquired or brought forth.

units.leftText: Again she gave birth, to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
units.rightText: Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel.

units.leftText: As time passed, Cain brought an offering to the LORD from the fruit of the ground.
units.rightText: So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD,

units.leftText: Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. The LORD respected Abel and his offering,
units.rightText: while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock.

units.leftText: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.
units.rightText: but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?
units.rightText: “Why are you angry,” said the LORD to Cain, “and why has your countenance fallen?

units.leftText: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”
units.rightText: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”
rightNotes: 4:7 Or it desires to control you

units.leftText: Cain said to Abel, his brother, “Let’s go into the field.” While they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.
units.rightText: Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
rightNotes: 4:8 SP, LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew Then Cain spoke to his brother Abel.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Cain, “Where is Abel, your brother?”
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?”

units.leftText: The LORD said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.
units.rightText: “What have you done?” replied the LORD. “The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.

units.leftText: Now you are cursed because of the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
units.rightText: Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

units.leftText: From now on, when you till the ground, it won’t yield its strength to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”
units.rightText: When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”

units.leftText: Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.
units.rightText: But Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.
rightNotes: 4:13 Or guilt or sin

units.leftText: Behold, you have driven me out today from the surface of the ground. I will be hidden from your face, and I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth. Whoever finds me will kill me.”
units.rightText: Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”

units.leftText: The LORD said to him, “Therefore whoever slays Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.” The LORD appointed a sign for Cain, so that anyone finding him would not strike him.
units.rightText: “Not so!” replied the LORD. “If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold.” And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
rightNotes: 4:15 LXX, Vulgate, and Syriac; Hebrew “Very well!” or “Therefore:”

units.leftText: Cain left the LORD’s presence, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
units.rightText: So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
rightNotes: 4:16 Nod means wandering.

units.leftText: Cain knew his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city, and named the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
units.rightText: And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.

units.leftText: Irad was born to Enoch. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.
units.rightText: Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methusael, and Methusael was the father of Lamech.

units.leftText: Lamech took two wives: the name of the first one was Adah, and the name of the second one was Zillah.
units.rightText: And Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.

units.leftText: Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.
units.rightText: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.

units.leftText: His brother’s name was Jubal, who was the father of all who handle the harp and pipe.
units.rightText: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.

units.leftText: Zillah also gave birth to Tubal Cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron. Tubal Cain’s sister was Naamah.
units.rightText: And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.

units.leftText: Lamech said to his wives,
units.rightText: Then Lamech said to his wives:

units.leftText: If Cain will be avenged seven times,
units.rightText: If Cain is avenged sevenfold,

units.leftText: Adam knew his wife again. She gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, saying, “for God has given me another child instead of Abel, for Cain killed him.”
units.rightText: And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”
rightNotes: 4:25 Seth probably means granted or appointed.

units.leftText: A son was also born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. At that time men began to call on the LORD’s name.
units.rightText: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh.

units.leftText: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him in God’s likeness.
units.rightText: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, He made him in His own likeness.

units.leftText: He created them male and female, and blessed them. On the day they were created, he named them Adam.
units.rightText: Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. And in the day they were created, He called them “man.”
leftNotes: 5:2 “Adam” and “Man” are spelled with the exact same consonants in Hebrew, so this can be correctly translated either way.
rightNotes: 5:2 Cited in Matthew 19:4|MAT 19:4* and Mark 10:6
5:2 Hebrew Adam

units.leftText: Adam lived one hundred thirty years, and became the father of a son in his own likeness, after his image, and named him Seth.
units.rightText: When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image; and he named him Seth.

units.leftText: The days of Adam after he became the father of Seth were eight hundred years, and he became the father of other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Seth, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred thirty years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Seth lived one hundred five years, then became the father of Enosh.
units.rightText: When Seth was 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.

units.leftText: Seth lived after he became the father of Enosh eight hundred seven years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: All of the days of Seth were nine hundred twelve years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Enosh lived ninety years, and became the father of Kenan.
units.rightText: When Enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.

units.leftText: Enosh lived after he became the father of Kenan eight hundred fifteen years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: All of the days of Enosh were nine hundred five years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Kenan lived seventy years, then became the father of Mahalalel.
units.rightText: When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.

units.leftText: Kenan lived after he became the father of Mahalalel eight hundred forty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: and all of the days of Kenan were nine hundred ten years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Jared.
units.rightText: When Mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.

units.leftText: Mahalalel lived after he became the father of Jared eight hundred thirty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: All of the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred ninety-five years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Jared lived one hundred sixty-two years, then became the father of Enoch.
units.rightText: When Jared was 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.

units.leftText: Jared lived after he became the father of Enoch eight hundred years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: All of the days of Jared were nine hundred sixty-two years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Jared lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Enoch lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Methuselah.
units.rightText: When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.

units.leftText: After Methuselah’s birth, Enoch walked with God for three hundred years, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
rightNotes: 5:22 LXX pleased God; also in verse 24

units.leftText: All the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty-five years.
units.rightText: So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.

units.leftText: Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.
units.rightText: Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.
rightNotes: 5:24 LXX and he was not found, because God had taken him away; cited in Hebrews 11:5|HEB 11:5*

units.leftText: Methuselah lived one hundred eighty-seven years, then became the father of Lamech.
units.rightText: When Methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.

units.leftText: Methuselah lived after he became the father of Lamech seven hundred eighty-two years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty-nine years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Lamech lived one hundred eighty-two years, then became the father of a son.
units.rightText: When Lamech was 182 years old, he had a son.

units.leftText: He named him Noah, saying, “This one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands, caused by the ground which the LORD has cursed.”
units.rightText: And he named him Noah, saying, “May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed.”
rightNotes: 5:29 Noah sounds like the Hebrew for rest or comfort.

units.leftText: Lamech lived after he became the father of Noah five hundred ninety-five years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Noah, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: All the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy-seven years, then he died.
units.rightText: So Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Noah was five hundred years old, then Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
units.rightText: After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

units.leftText: When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters were born to them,
units.rightText: Now when men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them,

units.leftText: God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives.
units.rightText: the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took as wives whomever they chose.

units.leftText: The LORD said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.”
units.rightText: So the LORD said, “My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.”
rightNotes: 6:3 LXX and Syriac My Spirit will not remain in man forever

units.leftText: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also after that, when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children with them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown.
units.rightText: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days— and afterward as well— when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men. And they bore them children who became the mighty men of old, men of renown.

units.leftText: The LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great on the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.
units.rightText: Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.

units.leftText: The LORD was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
units.rightText: And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.

units.leftText: The LORD said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the surface of the ground—man, along with animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky—for I am sorry that I have made them.”
units.rightText: So the LORD said, “I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth — every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air — for I am grieved that I have made them.”

units.leftText: But Noah found favor in the LORD’s eyes.
units.rightText: Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.

units.leftText: This is the history of the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.
units.rightText: This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.

units.leftText: Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
units.rightText: And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

units.leftText: The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
units.rightText: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.

units.leftText: God saw the earth, and saw that it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.
units.rightText: And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.
rightNotes: 6:12 Literally all flesh; similarly in verses 13, 17, and 19

units.leftText: God said to Noah, “I will bring an end to all flesh, for the earth is filled with violence through them. Behold, I will destroy them and the earth.
units.rightText: Then God said to Noah, “The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.

units.leftText: Make a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship, and shall seal it inside and outside with pitch.
units.rightText: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
rightNotes: 6:14 Gopher is an unknown kind of tree; possibly cypress or cedar.

units.leftText: This is how you shall make it. The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
units.rightText: And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
leftNotes: 6:15 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.
rightNotes: 6:15 The ark was approximately 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high (137.2 meters long, 22.9 meters wide, and 13.7 meters high).

units.leftText: You shall make a roof in the ship, and you shall finish it to a cubit upward. You shall set the door of the ship in its side. You shall make it with lower, second, and third levels.
units.rightText: You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
rightNotes: 6:16 Or skylight or window
6:16 A cubit is approximately 18 inches or 45.7 centimeters.

units.leftText: I, even I, will bring the flood of waters on this earth, to destroy all flesh having the breath of life from under the sky. Everything that is on the earth will die.
units.rightText: And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.

units.leftText: But I will establish my covenant with you. You shall come into the ship, you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
units.rightText: But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark — you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.

units.leftText: Of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every sort into the ship, to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.
units.rightText: And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark — male and female — to keep them alive with you.

units.leftText: Of the birds after their kind, of the livestock after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every sort will come to you, to keep them alive.
units.rightText: Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.

units.leftText: Take with you some of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it will be for food for you, and for them.”
units.rightText: You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.”

units.leftText: Thus Noah did. He did all that God commanded him.
units.rightText: So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Noah, “Come with all of your household into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Noah, “Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.

units.leftText: You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you, the male and his female. Of the animals that are not clean, take two, the male and his female.
units.rightText: You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate; a pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate;
rightNotes: 7:2 Or by sevens; also in verse 3

units.leftText: Also of the birds of the sky, seven and seven, male and female, to keep seed alive on the surface of all the earth.
units.rightText: and seven pairs of every kind of bird of the air, male and female, to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.

units.leftText: In seven days, I will cause it to rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will destroy every living thing that I have made from the surface of the ground.”
units.rightText: For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living thing I have made.”

units.leftText: Noah did everything that the LORD commanded him.
units.rightText: And Noah did all that the LORD had commanded him.

units.leftText: Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came on the earth.
units.rightText: Now Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.

units.leftText: Noah went into the ship with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives, because of the floodwaters.
units.rightText: And Noah and his wife, with his sons and their wives, entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.

units.leftText: Clean animals, unclean animals, birds, and everything that creeps on the ground
units.rightText: The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground

units.leftText: went by pairs to Noah into the ship, male and female, as God commanded Noah.
units.rightText: came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.

units.leftText: After the seven days, the floodwaters came on the earth.
units.rightText: And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.

units.leftText: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the sky’s windows opened.
units.rightText: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.

units.leftText: It rained on the earth forty days and forty nights.
units.rightText: And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.

units.leftText: In the same day Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japheth—the sons of Noah—and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered into the ship—
units.rightText: On that very day Noah entered the ark, along with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and his wife, and the three wives of his sons —

units.leftText: they, and every animal after its kind, all the livestock after their kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.
units.rightText: they and every kind of wild animal, livestock, crawling creature, bird, and winged creature.

units.leftText: Pairs from all flesh with the breath of life in them went into the ship to Noah.
units.rightText: They came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two of every creature with the breath of life.
rightNotes: 7:15 Literally of all flesh; similarly in verses 16 and 21

units.leftText: Those who went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded him; then the LORD shut him in.
units.rightText: And they entered, the male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.

units.leftText: The flood was forty days on the earth. The waters increased, and lifted up the ship, and it was lifted up above the earth.
units.rightText: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.

units.leftText: The waters rose, and increased greatly on the earth; and the ship floated on the surface of the waters.
units.rightText: So the waters continued to surge and rise greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.

units.leftText: The waters rose very high on the earth. All the high mountains that were under the whole sky were covered.
units.rightText: Finally, the waters completely prevailed upon the earth, so that all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.

units.leftText: The waters rose fifteen cubits higher, and the mountains were covered.
units.rightText: The waters rose and covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.
leftNotes: 7:20 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.
rightNotes: 7:20 15 cubits is approximately 22.5 feet or 6.9 meters.

units.leftText: All flesh died that moved on the earth, including birds, livestock, animals, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and every man.
units.rightText: And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished — birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind.

units.leftText: All on the dry land, in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, died.
units.rightText: Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.

units.leftText: Every living thing was destroyed that was on the surface of the ground, including man, livestock, creeping things, and birds of the sky. They were destroyed from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those who were with him in the ship.
units.rightText: And every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed — man and livestock, crawling creatures and birds of the air; they were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.

units.leftText: The waters flooded the earth one hundred fifty days.
units.rightText: And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.

units.leftText: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided.
units.rightText: But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside.

units.leftText: The deep’s fountains and the sky’s windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
units.rightText: The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the sky was restrained.

units.leftText: The waters continually receded from the earth. After the end of one hundred fifty days the waters receded.
units.rightText: The waters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the waters had gone down.

units.leftText: The ship rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on Ararat’s mountains.
units.rightText: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

units.leftText: The waters receded continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were visible.
units.rightText: And the waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.

units.leftText: At the end of forty days, Noah opened the window of the ship which he had made,
units.rightText: After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark

units.leftText: and he sent out a raven. It went back and forth, until the waters were dried up from the earth.
units.rightText: and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.

units.leftText: He himself sent out a dove to see if the waters were abated from the surface of the ground,
units.rightText: Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.
rightNotes: 8:8 Literally sent out from him or sent out from it

units.leftText: but the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned into the ship to him, for the waters were on the surface of the whole earth. He put out his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ship.
units.rightText: But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth. So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark.

units.leftText: He waited yet another seven days; and again he sent the dove out of the ship.
units.rightText: Noah waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.

units.leftText: The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth.
units.rightText: And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.

units.leftText: He waited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove; and she didn’t return to him any more.
units.rightText: And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him.

units.leftText: In the six hundred first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ship, and looked. He saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
units.rightText: In Noah’s six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried up from the earth. So Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.

units.leftText: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
units.rightText: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was fully dry.

units.leftText: God spoke to Noah, saying,
units.rightText: Then God said to Noah,

units.leftText: “Go out of the ship, you, your wife, your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.
units.rightText: “Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives.

units.leftText: Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh, including birds, livestock, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, that they may breed abundantly on the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply on the earth.”
units.rightText: Bring out all the living creatures that are with you— birds, livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground— so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.”

units.leftText: Noah went out, with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives with him.
units.rightText: So Noah came out, along with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives.

units.leftText: Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird, whatever moves on the earth, after their families, went out of the ship.
units.rightText: Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird — everything that moves upon the earth — came out of the ark, kind by kind.

units.leftText: Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean animal, and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
units.rightText: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.

units.leftText: The LORD smelled the pleasant aroma. The LORD said in his heart, “I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth. I will never again strike every living thing, as I have done.
units.rightText: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart, “Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.

units.leftText: While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.”
units.rightText: As long as the earth endures,

units.leftText: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.
units.rightText: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

units.leftText: The fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky. Everything that moves along the ground, and all the fish of the sea, are delivered into your hand.
units.rightText: The fear and dread of you will fall on every living creature on the earth, every bird of the air, every creature that crawls on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. They are delivered into your hand.

units.leftText: Every moving thing that lives will be food for you. As I gave you the green herb, I have given everything to you.
units.rightText: Everything that lives and moves will be food for you; just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you all things.

units.leftText: But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.
units.rightText: But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.

units.leftText: I will surely require accounting for your life’s blood. At the hand of every animal I will require it. At the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, I will require the life of man.
units.rightText: And surely I will require the life of any man or beast by whose hand your lifeblood is shed. I will demand an accounting from anyone who takes the life of his fellow man:

units.leftText: Whoever sheds man’s blood, his blood will be shed by man, for God made man in his own image.
units.rightText: Whoever sheds the blood of man,

units.leftText: Be fruitful and multiply. Increase abundantly on the earth, and multiply in it.”
units.rightText: But as for you,

units.leftText: God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
units.rightText: Then God said to Noah and his sons with him,

units.leftText: “As for me, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you,
units.rightText: “Behold, I now establish My covenant with you and your descendants after you,

units.leftText: and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ship, even every animal of the earth.
units.rightText: and with every living creature that was with you — the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth— every living thing that came out of the ark.

units.leftText: I will establish my covenant with you: All flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
units.rightText: And I establish My covenant with you: Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.”

units.leftText: God said, “This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
units.rightText: And God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am making between Me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:

units.leftText: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
units.rightText: I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.

units.leftText: When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud,
units.rightText: Whenever I form clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,

units.leftText: I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
units.rightText: I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.

units.leftText: The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
units.rightText: And whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of every kind that is on the earth.”

units.leftText: God said to Noah, “This is the token of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth.”
units.rightText: So God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and every creature on the earth.”

units.leftText: The sons of Noah who went out from the ship were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham is the father of Canaan.
units.rightText: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And Ham was the father of Canaan.

units.leftText: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the whole earth was populated.
units.rightText: These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was populated.

units.leftText: Noah began to be a farmer, and planted a vineyard.
units.rightText: Now Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard.
rightNotes: 9:20 Or was the first

units.leftText: He drank of the wine and got drunk. He was uncovered within his tent.
units.rightText: But when he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and uncovered himself inside his tent.

units.leftText: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.
units.rightText: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father’s nakedness and told his two brothers outside.

units.leftText: Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it on both their shoulders, went in backwards, and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were backwards, and they didn’t see their father’s nakedness.
units.rightText: Then Shem and Japheth took a garment and placed it across their shoulders, and walking backward, they covered their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned away so that they did not see their father’s nakedness.

units.leftText: Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
units.rightText: When Noah awoke from his drunkenness and learned what his youngest son had done to him,

units.leftText: He said,
units.rightText: he said,

units.leftText: He said,
units.rightText: He also declared:

units.leftText: May God enlarge Japheth.
units.rightText: May God expand the territory of Japheth;
rightNotes: 9:27 Japheth sounds like the Hebrew for expand.

units.leftText: Noah lived three hundred fifty years after the flood.
units.rightText: After the flood, Noah lived 350 years.

units.leftText: All the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, and then he died.
units.rightText: So Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.

units.leftText: Now this is the history of the generations of the sons of Noah and of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
units.rightText: This is the account of Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, who also had sons after the flood.

units.leftText: The sons of Japheth were: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
units.rightText: The sons of Japheth:

units.leftText: The sons of Gomer were: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
units.rightText: The sons of Gomer:

units.leftText: The sons of Javan were: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
units.rightText: And the sons of Javan:

units.leftText: Of these were the islands of the nations divided in their lands, everyone after his language, after their families, in their nations.
units.rightText: From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, according to their languages, by clans within their nations.

units.leftText: The sons of Ham were: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
units.rightText: The sons of Ham:

units.leftText: The sons of Cush were: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were: Sheba and Dedan.
units.rightText: The sons of Cush:

units.leftText: Cush became the father of Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one on the earth.
units.rightText: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.
rightNotes: 10:8 Or who established himself as a mighty warrior or who became the first fearless leader

units.leftText: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD. Therefore it is said, “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD”.
units.rightText: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; so it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.”
rightNotes: 10:9 Or in defiance of; twice in this verse

units.leftText: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
units.rightText: His kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
rightNotes: 10:10 That is, Babylonia

units.leftText: Out of that land he went into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah,
units.rightText: From that land he went forth into Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,

units.leftText: and Resen between Nineveh and the great city Calah.
units.rightText: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and the great city of Calah.

units.leftText: Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
units.rightText: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,

units.leftText: Pathrusim, Casluhim (which the Philistines descended from), and Caphtorim.
units.rightText: the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites.
rightNotes: 10:14 Some translators adjust the Hebrew word order to the Casluhites, and the Caphtorites (from whom the Philistines came); see also Jeremiah 47:4|JER 47:4* and Amos 9:7.

units.leftText: Canaan became the father of Sidon (his firstborn), Heth,
units.rightText: And Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
rightNotes: 10:15 Or of the Sidonians, the foremost

units.leftText: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
units.rightText: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

units.leftText: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
units.rightText: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

units.leftText: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad.
units.rightText: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.

units.leftText: The border of the Canaanites was from Sidon—as you go toward Gerar—to Gaza—as you go toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim—to Lasha.
units.rightText: and the borders of Canaan extended from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Ham, after their families, according to their languages, in their lands and their nations.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Ham according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.

units.leftText: Children were also born to Shem (the elder brother of Japheth), the father of all the children of Eber.
units.rightText: And sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth; Shem was the forefather of all the sons of Eber.
rightNotes: 10:21 Or Shem, whose older brother was Japheth

units.leftText: The sons of Shem were: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
units.rightText: The sons of Shem:

units.leftText: The sons of Aram were: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
units.rightText: The sons of Aram:

units.leftText: Arpachshad became the father of Shelah. Shelah became the father of Eber.
units.rightText: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
rightNotes: 10:24 Hebrew; LXX (see also Luke 3:35–36|LUK 3:35-36*) And Arphaxad was the father of Cainan, and Cainan was the father of Shelah,

units.leftText: To Eber were born two sons. The name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided. His brother’s name was Joktan.
units.rightText: Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.
rightNotes: 10:25 Peleg means division.

units.leftText: Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
units.rightText: And Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

units.leftText: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
units.rightText: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

units.leftText: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
units.rightText: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,

units.leftText: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
units.rightText: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.

units.leftText: Their dwelling extended from Mesha, as you go toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
units.rightText: Their territory extended from Mesha to Sephar, in the eastern hill country.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Shem, by their families, according to their languages, lands, and nations.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Shem, according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.

units.leftText: These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, according to their nations. The nations divided from these on the earth after the flood.
units.rightText: All these are the clans of Noah’s sons, according to their generations and nations. From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood.

units.leftText: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech.
units.rightText: Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.

units.leftText: As they traveled east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they lived there.
units.rightText: And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
rightNotes: 11:2 Or from the east or in the east
11:2 That is, Babylonia

units.leftText: They said to one another, “Come, let’s make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar.
units.rightText: And they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.” So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.

units.leftText: They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.”
units.rightText: “Come,” they said, “let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.”

units.leftText: The LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men built.
units.rightText: Then the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.

units.leftText: The LORD said, “Behold, they are one people, and they all have one language, and this is what they begin to do. Now nothing will be withheld from them, which they intend to do.
units.rightText: And the LORD said, “If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.

units.leftText: Come, let’s go down, and there confuse their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.”
units.rightText: Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”

units.leftText: So the LORD scattered them abroad from there on the surface of all the earth. They stopped building the city.
units.rightText: So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.

units.leftText: Therefore its name was called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of all the earth. From there, the LORD scattered them abroad on the surface of all the earth.
units.rightText: That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth.
rightNotes: 11:9 Or Babylon; the Hebrew word for Babel sounds like the Hebrew for confused.

units.leftText: This is the history of the generations of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old when he became the father of Arpachshad two years after the flood.
units.rightText: This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.

units.leftText: Shem lived five hundred years after he became the father of Arpachshad, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and became the father of Shelah.
units.rightText: When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shelah.

units.leftText: Arpachshad lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Shelah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Shelah, Arphaxad lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
rightNotes: 11:13 Hebrew; LXX (see also Luke 3:35–36|LUK 3:35-36*) 12*When Arphaxad was 135 years old, he became the father of Cainan. 13*And after he had become the father of Cainan, Arphaxad lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters, and then he died. When Cainan had lived 130 years, he became the father of Shelah. And after he had become the father of Shelah, Cainan lived 330 years and had other sons and daughters.Note that LXX also adds 100 years to the ages of Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, and Nahor in this genealogy.

units.leftText: Shelah lived thirty years, and became the father of Eber.
units.rightText: When Shelah was 30 years old, he became the father of Eber.

units.leftText: Shelah lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Eber, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Eber, Shelah lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: Eber lived thirty-four years, and became the father of Peleg.
units.rightText: When Eber was 34 years old, he became the father of Peleg.

units.leftText: Eber lived four hundred thirty years after he became the father of Peleg, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Peleg, Eber lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: Peleg lived thirty years, and became the father of Reu.
units.rightText: When Peleg was 30 years old, he became the father of Reu.

units.leftText: Peleg lived two hundred nine years after he became the father of Reu, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: Reu lived thirty-two years, and became the father of Serug.
units.rightText: When Reu was 32 years old, he became the father of Serug.

units.leftText: Reu lived two hundred seven years after he became the father of Serug, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Serug, Reu lived 207 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: Serug lived thirty years, and became the father of Nahor.
units.rightText: When Serug was 30 years old, he became the father of Nahor.

units.leftText: Serug lived two hundred years after he became the father of Nahor, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Nahor, Serug lived 200 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and became the father of Terah.
units.rightText: When Nahor was 29 years old, he became the father of Terah.

units.leftText: Nahor lived one hundred nineteen years after he became the father of Terah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And after he had become the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years and had other sons and daughters.

units.leftText: Terah lived seventy years, and became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
units.rightText: When Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

units.leftText: Now this is the history of the generations of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran became the father of Lot.
units.rightText: This is the account of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. And Haran became the father of Lot.

units.leftText: Haran died in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldees, while his father Terah was still alive.
units.rightText: During his father Terah’s lifetime, Haran died in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans.

units.leftText: Abram and Nahor married wives. The name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, who was also the father of Iscah.
units.rightText: And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarai, and Nahor’s wife was named Milcah; she was the daughter of Haran, who was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.

units.leftText: Sarai was barren. She had no child.
units.rightText: But Sarai was barren; she had no children.

units.leftText: Terah took Abram his son, Lot the son of Haran, his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram’s wife. They went from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan. They came to Haran and lived there.
units.rightText: And Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai the wife of Abram, and they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans for the land of Canaan. But when they arrived in Haran, they settled there.

units.leftText: The days of Terah were two hundred five years. Terah died in Haran.
units.rightText: Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.

units.leftText: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household, and go to the land I will show you.
rightNotes: 12:1 Cited in Acts 7:3|ACT 7:3*

units.leftText: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.
units.rightText: I will make you into a great nation,

units.leftText: I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
units.rightText: I will bless those who bless you

units.leftText: So Abram went, as the LORD had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
units.rightText: So Abram departed, as the LORD had directed him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

units.leftText: Abram took Sarai his wife, Lot his brother’s son, all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people whom they had acquired in Haran, and they went to go into the land of Canaan. They entered into the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran, and set out for the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time, Canaanites were in the land.
units.rightText: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.
rightNotes: 12:6 Or Terebinth or Great Tree

units.leftText: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring. ” So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
rightNotes: 12:7 Cited in Galatians 3:16|GAL 3:16*
