units.leftText: He left from there to go to the mountain on the east of Bethel and pitched his tent, having Bethel on the west, and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the LORD’s name.
units.rightText: From there Abram moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD, and he called on the name of the LORD.
leftNotes: 12:8 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: Abram traveled, still going on toward the South.
units.rightText: And Abram journeyed on toward the Negev.

units.leftText: There was a famine in the land. Abram went down into Egypt to live as a foreigner there, for the famine was severe in the land.
units.rightText: Now there was a famine in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.

units.leftText: When he had come near to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “See now, I know that you are a beautiful woman to look at.
units.rightText: As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, “Look, I know that you are a beautiful woman,

units.leftText: It will happen that when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ They will kill me, but they will save you alive.
units.rightText: and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ Then they will kill me but will let you live.

units.leftText: Please say that you are my sister, that it may be well with me for your sake, and that my soul may live because of you.”
units.rightText: Please say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake, and on account of you my life will be spared.”

units.leftText: When Abram had come into Egypt, some Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
units.rightText: So when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.

units.leftText: The princes of Pharaoh saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
units.rightText: When Pharaoh’s officials saw Sarai, they commended her to him, and she was taken into the palace of Pharaoh.

units.leftText: He dealt well with Abram for her sake. He had sheep, cattle, male donkeys, male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
units.rightText: He treated Abram well on her account, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels.

units.leftText: The LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
units.rightText: The LORD, however, afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram’s wife Sarai.

units.leftText: Pharaoh called Abram and said, “What is this that you have done to me? Why didn’t you tell me that she was your wife?
units.rightText: So Pharaoh summoned Abram and asked, “What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?

units.leftText: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her to be my wife? Now therefore, see your wife, take her, and go your way.”
units.rightText: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!”

units.leftText: Pharaoh commanded men concerning him, and they escorted him away with his wife and all that he had.
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh gave his men orders concerning Abram, and they sent him away with his wife and all his possessions.

units.leftText: Abram went up out of Egypt—he, his wife, all that he had, and Lot with him—into the South.
units.rightText: So Abram went up out of Egypt into the Negev— he and his wife and all his possessions— and Lot was with him.

units.leftText: Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
units.rightText: And Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold.

units.leftText: He went on his journeys from the South as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
units.rightText: From the Negev he journeyed from place to place toward Bethel, until he came to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had formerly been pitched,

units.leftText: to the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first. There Abram called on the LORD’s name.
units.rightText: to the site where he had built the altar. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.

units.leftText: Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, herds, and tents.
units.rightText: Now Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.

units.leftText: The land was not able to bear them, that they might live together; for their possessions were so great that they couldn’t live together.
units.rightText: But the land was unable to support both of them while they stayed together, for they had so many possessions that they were unable to coexist.

units.leftText: There was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. The Canaanites and the Perizzites lived in the land at that time.
units.rightText: And there was discord between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also living in the land.

units.leftText: Abram said to Lot, “Please, let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herdsmen and my herdsmen; for we are relatives.
units.rightText: So Abram said to Lot, “Please let there be no contention between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen. After all, we are kinsmen.

units.leftText: Isn’t the whole land before you? Please separate yourself from me. If you go to the left hand, then I will go to the right. Or if you go to the right hand, then I will go to the left.”
units.rightText: Is not the whole land before you? Now separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.”

units.leftText: Lot lifted up his eyes, and saw all the plain of the Jordan, that it was well-watered everywhere, before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, as you go to Zoar.
units.rightText: And Lot looked out and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, was well watered like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)

units.leftText: So Lot chose the Plain of the Jordan for himself. Lot traveled east, and they separated themselves from one another.
units.rightText: So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself and set out toward the east. And Abram and Lot parted company.

units.leftText: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
units.rightText: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, but Lot settled in the cities of the plain and pitched his tent toward Sodom.

units.leftText: Now the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinners against the LORD.
units.rightText: But the men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, “Now, lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,
units.rightText: After Lot had departed, the LORD said to Abram, “Now lift up your eyes from the place where you are, and look to the north and south and east and west,

units.leftText: for I will give all the land which you see to you and to your offspring forever.
units.rightText: for all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever.
rightNotes: 13:15 Cited in Galatians 3:16|GAL 3:16*

units.leftText: I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth, so that if a man can count the dust of the earth, then your offspring may also be counted.
units.rightText: I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if one could count the dust of the earth, then your offspring could be counted.

units.leftText: Arise, walk through the land in its length and in its width; for I will give it to you.”
units.rightText: Get up and walk around the land, through its length and breadth, for I will give it to you.”

units.leftText: Abram moved his tent, and came and lived by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built an altar there to the LORD.
units.rightText: So Abram moved his tent and went to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to the LORD.
rightNotes: 13:18 Or Terebinths or Great Trees

units.leftText: In the days of Amraphel, king of Shinar; Arioch, king of Ellasar; Chedorlaomer, king of Elam; and Tidal, king of Goiim,
units.rightText: In those days Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim
rightNotes: 14:1 That is, Babylonia; also in verse 9

units.leftText: they made war with Bera, king of Sodom; Birsha, king of Gomorrah; Shinab, king of Admah; Shemeber, king of Zeboiim; and the king of Bela (also called Zoar).
units.rightText: went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).

units.leftText: All these joined together in the valley of Siddim (also called the Salt Sea).
units.rightText: The latter five came as allies to the Valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea ).
rightNotes: 14:3 That is, the Dead Sea

units.leftText: They served Chedorlaomer for twelve years, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
units.rightText: For twelve years they had been subject to Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

units.leftText: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him came and struck the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
units.rightText: In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him went out and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim,

units.leftText: and the Horites in their Mount Seir, to El Paran, which is by the wilderness.
units.rightText: and the Horites in the area of Mount Seir, as far as El-paran, which is near the desert.

units.leftText: They returned, and came to En Mishpat (also called Kadesh), and struck all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that lived in Hazazon Tamar.
units.rightText: Then they turned back to invade En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and they conquered the whole territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.

units.leftText: The king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (also called Zoar) went out; and they set the battle in array against them in the valley of Siddim
units.rightText: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) marched out and arrayed themselves for battle in the Valley of Siddim
rightNotes: 14:8 That is, the Valley of the Dead Sea

units.leftText: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings against the five.
units.rightText: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar— four kings against five.

units.leftText: Now the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and some fell there. Those who remained fled to the hills.
units.rightText: Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some men fell into the pits, but the survivors fled to the hill country.

units.leftText: They took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their food, and went their way.
units.rightText: The four kings seized all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and they went on their way.

units.leftText: They took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who lived in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.
units.rightText: They also carried off Abram’s nephew Lot and his possessions, since Lot was living in Sodom.

units.leftText: One who had escaped came and told Abram, the Hebrew. At that time, he lived by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner. They were allies of Abram.
units.rightText: Then an escapee came and reported this to Abram the Hebrew. Now Abram was living near the Oaks of Mamre the Amorite, a brother of Eshcol and Aner, all of whom were bound by treaty to Abram.
rightNotes: 14:13 Or Terebinths or Great Trees
14:13 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.

units.leftText: When Abram heard that his relative was taken captive, he led out his three hundred eighteen trained men, born in his house, and pursued as far as Dan.
units.rightText: And when Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he mobilized the 318 trained men born in his household, and they set out in pursuit as far as Dan.

units.leftText: He divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and struck them, and pursued them to Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.
units.rightText: During the night, Abram divided his forces and routed Chedorlaomer’s army, pursuing them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.

units.leftText: He brought back all the goods, and also brought back his relative Lot and his goods, and the women also, and the other people.
units.rightText: He retrieved all the goods, as well as his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the rest of the people.

units.leftText: The king of Sodom went out to meet him after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, at the valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley).
units.rightText: After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley).

units.leftText: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.
units.rightText: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine — since he was priest of God Most High —
rightNotes: 14:18 Hebrew El-Elyon; also in verses 19, 20, and 22; cited in Hebrews 7:1|HEB 7:1*

units.leftText: He blessed him, and said, “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth.
units.rightText: and he blessed Abram and said:

units.leftText: Blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.”
units.rightText: and blessed be God Most High,

units.leftText: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself.”
units.rightText: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, but take the goods for yourself.”

units.leftText: Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have lifted up my hand to the LORD, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,
units.rightText: But Abram replied to the king of Sodom, “I have raised my hand to the LORD God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,

units.leftText: that I will not take a thread nor a sandal strap nor anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
units.rightText: that I will not accept even a thread, or a strap of a sandal, or anything that belongs to you, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’

units.leftText: I will accept nothing from you except that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their portion.”
units.rightText: I will accept nothing but what my men have eaten and the share for the men who went with me— Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. They may take their portion.”

units.leftText: After these things the LORD’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
units.rightText: After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision:

units.leftText: Abram said, “Lord GOD, what will you give me, since I go childless, and he who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?”
units.rightText: But Abram replied, “O Lord GOD, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?”

units.leftText: Abram said, “Behold, you have given no children to me: and, behold, one born in my house is my heir.”
units.rightText: Abram continued, “Behold, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir.”

units.leftText: Behold, the LORD’s word came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir, but he who will come out of your own body will be your heir.”
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came to Abram, saying, “This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.”

units.leftText: The LORD brought him outside, and said, “Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” He said to Abram, “So your offspring will be.”
units.rightText: And the LORD took him outside and said, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.”
rightNotes: 15:5 Cited in Romans 4:18|ROM 4:18*

units.leftText: He believed in the LORD, who credited it to him for righteousness.
units.rightText: Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
rightNotes: 15:6 Cited in Romans 4:3|ROM 4:3*, Romans 4:22, Galatians 3:6, and James 2:23

units.leftText: He said to Abram, “I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you this land to inherit it.”
units.rightText: The LORD also told him, “I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.”

units.leftText: He said, “Lord GOD, how will I know that I will inherit it?”
units.rightText: But Abram replied, “Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?”

units.leftText: He said to him, “Bring me a heifer three years old, a female goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”
units.rightText: And the LORD said to him, “Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon.”

units.leftText: He brought him all these, and divided them in the middle, and laid each half opposite the other; but he didn’t divide the birds.
units.rightText: So Abram brought all these to Him, split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other. The birds, however, he did not cut in half.

units.leftText: The birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
units.rightText: And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.

units.leftText: When the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. Now terror and great darkness fell on him.
units.rightText: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him.

units.leftText: He said to Abram, “Know for sure that your offspring will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

units.leftText: I will also judge that nation, whom they will serve. Afterward they will come out with great wealth;
units.rightText: But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will depart with many possessions.
rightNotes: 15:14 Cited in Acts 7:6–7|ACT 7:6-7*

units.leftText: but you will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age.
units.rightText: You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.

units.leftText: In the fourth generation they will come here again, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full.”
units.rightText: In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”

units.leftText: It came to pass that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.
units.rightText: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses.

units.leftText: In that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “I have given this land to your offspring, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
units.rightText: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I have given this land — from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates —

units.leftText: the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
units.rightText: the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,

units.leftText: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
units.rightText: Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,

units.leftText: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”
units.rightText: Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.”

units.leftText: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, bore him no children. She had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.
units.rightText: Now Abram’s wife Sarai had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.

units.leftText: Sarai said to Abram, “See now, the LORD has restrained me from bearing. Please go in to my servant. It may be that I will obtain children by her.” Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
units.rightText: So Sarai said to Abram, “Look now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.”

units.leftText: Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.
units.rightText: So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to Abram to be his wife.

units.leftText: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
units.rightText: And he slept with Hagar, and she conceived. But when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.
rightNotes: 16:4 Or her mistress became despised in her sight

units.leftText: Sarai said to Abram, “This wrong is your fault. I gave my servant into your bosom, and when she saw that she had conceived, she despised me. May the LORD judge between me and you.”
units.rightText: Then Sarai said to Abram, “May the wrong done to me be upon you! I delivered my servant into your arms, and ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me.”

units.leftText: But Abram said to Sarai, “Behold, your maid is in your hand. Do to her whatever is good in your eyes.” Sarai dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her face.
units.rightText: “Here,” said Abram, “your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain on the way to Shur.
units.rightText: Now the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert — the spring along the road to Shur.
rightNotes: 16:7 Or Angel; also in verses 9, 10, and 11; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.

units.leftText: He said, “Hagar, Sarai’s servant, where did you come from? Where are you going?”
units.rightText: “Hagar, servant of Sarai,” he said, “where have you come from, and where are you going?”

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands.”
units.rightText: So the angel of the LORD told her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.”

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to her, “I will greatly multiply your offspring, that they will not be counted for multitude.”
units.rightText: Then the angel added, “I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.”

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to her, “Behold, you are with child, and will bear a son. You shall call his name Ishmael, because the LORD has heard your affliction.
units.rightText: The angel of the LORD proceeded:

units.leftText: He will be like a wild donkey among men. His hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him. He will live opposed to all of his brothers.”
units.rightText: He will be a wild donkey of a man,

units.leftText: She called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”
units.rightText: So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her: “You are the God who sees me, ” for she said, “Here I have seen the One who sees me!”
rightNotes: 16:13 Hebrew El-Roi

units.leftText: Therefore the well was called Beer Lahai Roi. Behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
units.rightText: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is located between Kadesh and Bered.
leftNotes: 16:14 Beer Lahai Roi means “well of the one who lives and sees me”.
rightNotes: 16:14 Beer-lahai-roi means well of the Living One who sees me.

units.leftText: Hagar bore a son for Abram. Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
units.rightText: And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.

units.leftText: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
units.rightText: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.

units.leftText: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.
units.rightText: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.
rightNotes: 17:1 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: I will make my covenant between me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.”
units.rightText: I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”

units.leftText: Abram fell on his face. God talked with him, saying,
units.rightText: Then Abram fell facedown, and God said to him,

units.leftText: “As for me, behold, my covenant is with you. You will be the father of a multitude of nations.
units.rightText: “As for Me, this is My covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.

units.leftText: Your name will no more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
units.rightText: No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.
rightNotes: 17:5 Abram means exalted father.
17:5 Abraham means father of many.
17:5 Cited in Romans 4:17|ROM 4:17*

units.leftText: I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you. Kings will come out of you.
units.rightText: I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will descend from you.

units.leftText: I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your offspring after you.
units.rightText: I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.

units.leftText: I will give to you, and to your offspring after you, the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. I will be their God.”
units.rightText: And to you and your descendants I will give the land where you are residing— all the land of Canaan— as an eternal possession; and I will be their God.”

units.leftText: God said to Abraham, “As for you, you shall keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you throughout their generations.
units.rightText: God also said to Abraham, “You must keep My covenant— you and your descendants in the generations after you.

units.leftText: This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your offspring after you. Every male among you shall be circumcised.
units.rightText: This is My covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you are to keep: Every male among you must be circumcised.

units.leftText: You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin. It will be a token of the covenant between me and you.
units.rightText: You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

units.leftText: He who is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he who is born in the house, or bought with money from any foreigner who is not of your offspring.
units.rightText: Generation after generation, every male must be circumcised when he is eight days old, including those born in your household and those purchased from a foreigner — even those who are not your offspring.

units.leftText: He who is born in your house, and he who is bought with your money, must be circumcised. My covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
units.rightText: Whether they are born in your household or purchased, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh will be an everlasting covenant.

units.leftText: The uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people. He has broken my covenant.”
units.rightText: But if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.”

units.leftText: God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but her name shall be Sarah.
units.rightText: Then God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, do not call her Sarai, for her name is to be Sarah.
rightNotes: 17:15 Both Sarai and Sarah mean princess; the change in spelling may reflect the difference in dialect between Ur and Canaan.

units.leftText: I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. Yes, I will bless her, and she will be a mother of nations. Kings of peoples will come from her.”
units.rightText: And I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will descend from her.”

units.leftText: Then Abraham fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, “Will a child be born to him who is one hundred years old? Will Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?”
units.rightText: Abraham fell facedown. Then he laughed and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?”

units.leftText: Abraham said to God, “Oh that Ishmael might live before you!”
units.rightText: And Abraham said to God, “O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!”

units.leftText: God said, “No, but Sarah, your wife, will bear you a son. You shall call his name Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.
units.rightText: But God replied, “Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son, and you are to name him Isaac. I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
rightNotes: 17:19 Isaac means he laughs.

units.leftText: As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly. He will become the father of twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
units.rightText: As for Ishmael, I have heard you, and I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will become the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.

units.leftText: But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this set time next year.”
units.rightText: But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”

units.leftText: When he finished talking with him, God went up from Abraham.
units.rightText: When He had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.

units.leftText: Abraham took Ishmael his son, all who were born in his house, and all who were bought with his money: every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the same day, as God had said to him.
units.rightText: On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household or purchased with his money— every male among the members of Abraham’s household— and he circumcised them, just as God had told him.

units.leftText: Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
units.rightText: So Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,

units.leftText: Ishmael, his son, was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
units.rightText: and his son Ishmael was thirteen;

units.leftText: In the same day both Abraham and Ishmael, his son, were circumcised.
units.rightText: Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.

units.leftText: All the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with money from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
units.rightText: And all the men of Abraham’s household— both servants born in his household and those purchased from foreigners— were circumcised with him.

units.leftText: The LORD appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.
units.rightText: Then the LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent.
rightNotes: 18:1 Or Terebinths or Great Trees

units.leftText: He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood near him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,
units.rightText: And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.

units.leftText: and said, “My lord, if now I have found favor in your sight, please don’t go away from your servant.
units.rightText: “My lord,” said Abraham, “if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.

units.leftText: Now let a little water be fetched, wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
units.rightText: Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.

units.leftText: I will get a piece of bread so you can refresh your heart. After that you may go your way, now that you have come to your servant.”
units.rightText: And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. This is why you have passed your servant’s way. After that, you may continue on your way.”

units.leftText: Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said, “Quickly prepare three seahs of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.”
units.rightText: So Abraham hurried into the tent and said to Sarah, “Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread.”
leftNotes: 18:6 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks
rightNotes: 18:6 3 seahs is approximately 19.8 dry quarts or 21.9 liters (probably about 24.5 pounds or 11.1 kilograms of flour).

units.leftText: Abraham ran to the herd, and fetched a tender and good calf, and gave it to the servant. He hurried to dress it.
units.rightText: Meanwhile, Abraham ran to the herd, selected a tender and choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.

units.leftText: He took butter, milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them. He stood by them under the tree, and they ate.
units.rightText: Then Abraham brought curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and he set them before the men and stood by them under the tree as they ate.

units.leftText: They asked him, “Where is Sarah, your wife?”
units.rightText: “Where is your wife Sarah?” they asked.

units.leftText: He said, “I will certainly return to you at about this time next year; and behold, Sarah your wife will have a son.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD said, “I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!”

units.leftText: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age. Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
units.rightText: And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years; Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.

units.leftText: Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”
units.rightText: So she laughed to herself, saying, “After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?”

units.leftText: The LORD said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Will I really bear a child when I am old?’
units.rightText: And the LORD asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Can I really bear a child when I am old?’

units.leftText: Is anything too hard for the LORD? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes around, and Sarah will have a son.”
units.rightText: Is anything too difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you — in about a year — and Sarah will have a son.”
rightNotes: 18:14 Cited in Romans 9:9|ROM 9:9*

units.leftText: Then Sarah denied it, saying, “I didn’t laugh,” for she was afraid.
units.rightText: But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, “I did not laugh.”

units.leftText: The men rose up from there, and looked toward Sodom. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
units.rightText: When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.

units.leftText: The LORD said, “Will I hide from Abraham what I do,
units.rightText: And the LORD said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?

units.leftText: since Abraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him?
units.rightText: Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.

units.leftText: For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that the LORD may bring on Abraham that which he has spoken of him.”
units.rightText: For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has promised.”

units.leftText: The LORD said, “Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said, “The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous,

units.leftText: I will go down now, and see whether their deeds are as bad as the reports which have come to me. If not, I will know.”
units.rightText: I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out.”

units.leftText: The men turned from there, and went toward Sodom, but Abraham stood yet before the LORD.
units.rightText: And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.

units.leftText: Abraham came near, and said, “Will you consume the righteous with the wicked?
units.rightText: Abraham stepped forward and said, “Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?

units.leftText: What if there are fifty righteous within the city? Will you consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous who are in it?
units.rightText: What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?

units.leftText: May it be far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”
units.rightText: Far be it from You to do such a thing — to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”

units.leftText: The LORD said, “If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
units.rightText: So the LORD replied, “If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place.”

units.leftText: Abraham answered, “See now, I have taken it on myself to speak to the Lord, although I am dust and ashes.
units.rightText: Then Abraham answered, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord— though I am but dust and ashes—

units.leftText: What if there will lack five of the fifty righteous? Will you destroy all the city for lack of five?”
units.rightText: suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?”

units.leftText: He spoke to him yet again, and said, “What if there are forty found there?”
units.rightText: Once again Abraham spoke to the LORD, “Suppose forty are found there?”

units.leftText: He said, “Oh don’t let the Lord be angry, and I will speak. What if there are thirty found there?”
units.rightText: Then Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?”

units.leftText: He said, “See now, I have taken it on myself to speak to the Lord. What if there are twenty found there?”
units.rightText: And Abraham said, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?”

units.leftText: He said, “Oh don’t let the Lord be angry, and I will speak just once more. What if ten are found there?”
units.rightText: Finally, Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?”

units.leftText: The LORD went his way as soon as he had finished communing with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.
units.rightText: When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.

units.leftText: The two angels came to Sodom at evening. Lot sat in the gate of Sodom. Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them. He bowed himself with his face to the earth,
units.rightText: Now the two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them, bowed facedown,

units.leftText: and he said, “See now, my lords, please come into your servant’s house, stay all night, wash your feet, and you can rise up early, and go on your way.”
units.rightText: and said, “My lords, please turn aside into the house of your servant; wash your feet and spend the night. Then you can rise early and go on your way.”

units.leftText: He urged them greatly, and they came in with him, and entered into his house. He made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
units.rightText: But Lot insisted so strongly that they followed him into his house. He prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

units.leftText: But before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, both young and old, all the people from every quarter.
units.rightText: Before they had gone to bed, all the men of the city of Sodom, both young and old, surrounded the house.

units.leftText: They called to Lot, and said to him, “Where are the men who came in to you this night? Bring them out to us, that we may have sex with them.”
units.rightText: They called out to Lot, saying, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Send them out to us so we can have relations with them!”

units.leftText: Lot went out to them through the door, and shut the door after himself.
units.rightText: Lot went outside to meet them, shutting the door behind him.

units.leftText: He said, “Please, my brothers, don’t act so wickedly.
units.rightText: “Please, my brothers,” he pleaded, “don’t do such a wicked thing!

units.leftText: See now, I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them what seems good to you. Only don’t do anything to these men, because they have come under the shadow of my roof.”
units.rightText: Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them to you, and you can do to them as you please. But do not do anything to these men, for they have come under the protection of my roof.”

units.leftText: They said, “Stand back!” Then they said, “This one fellow came in to live as a foreigner, and he appoints himself a judge. Now we will deal worse with you than with them!” They pressed hard on the man Lot, and came near to break the door.
units.rightText: “Get out of the way!” they replied. And they declared, “This one came here as a foreigner, and he is already acting like a judge! Now we will treat you worse than them.” And they pressed in on Lot and moved in to break down the door.

units.leftText: But the men reached out their hand, and brought Lot into the house to them, and shut the door.
units.rightText: But the men inside reached out, pulled Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.

units.leftText: They struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.
units.rightText: And they struck the men at the entrance, young and old, with blindness, so that they wearied themselves trying to find the door.

units.leftText: The men said to Lot, “Do you have anybody else here? Sons-in-law, your sons, your daughters, and whomever you have in the city, bring them out of the place:
units.rightText: Then the two men said to Lot, “Do you have anyone else here — a son-in-law, your sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here,

units.leftText: for we will destroy this place, because the outcry against them has grown so great before the LORD that the LORD has sent us to destroy it.”
units.rightText: because we are about to destroy this place. For the outcry to the LORD against its people is so great that He has sent us to destroy it.”

units.leftText: Lot went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters, and said, “Get up! Get out of this place, for the LORD will destroy the city!”
units.rightText: So Lot went out and spoke to the sons-in-law who were pledged in marriage to his daughters. “Get up,” he said. “Get out of this place, for the LORD is about to destroy the city!” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.

units.leftText: When the morning came, then the angels hurried Lot, saying, “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, lest you be consumed in the iniquity of the city.”
units.rightText: At daybreak the angels hurried Lot along, saying, “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city.”

units.leftText: But he lingered; and the men grabbed his hand, his wife’s hand, and his two daughters’ hands, the LORD being merciful to him; and they took him out, and set him outside of the city.
units.rightText: But when Lot hesitated, the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters. And they led them safely out of the city, because of the LORD’s compassion for them.

units.leftText: It came to pass, when they had taken them out, that he said, “Escape for your life! Don’t look behind you, and don’t stay anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountains, lest you be consumed!”
units.rightText: As soon as the men had brought them out, one of them said, “Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere on the plain! Flee to the mountains, or you will be swept away!”

units.leftText: Lot said to them, “Oh, not so, my lord.
units.rightText: But Lot replied, “No, my lords, please!

units.leftText: See now, your servant has found favor in your sight, and you have magnified your loving kindness, which you have shown to me in saving my life. I can’t escape to the mountain, lest evil overtake me, and I die.
units.rightText: Your servant has indeed found favor in your sight, and you have shown me great kindness by sparing my life. But I cannot run to the mountains; the disaster will overtake me, and I will die.

units.leftText: See now, this city is near to flee to, and it is a little one. Oh let me escape there (isn’t it a little one?), and my soul will live.”
units.rightText: Look, there is a town nearby where I can flee, and it is a small place. Please let me flee there — is it not a small place? Then my life will be saved.”

units.leftText: He said to him, “Behold, I have granted your request concerning this thing also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
units.rightText: “Very well,” he answered, “I will grant this request as well, and will not demolish the town you indicate.

units.leftText: Hurry, escape there, for I can’t do anything until you get there.” Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.
units.rightText: Hurry! Run there quickly, for I cannot do anything until you reach it.” That is why the town was called Zoar.
rightNotes: 19:22 Zoar means small.

units.leftText: The sun had risen on the earth when Lot came to Zoar.
units.rightText: And by the time the sun had risen over the land, Lot had reached Zoar.

units.leftText: Then the LORD rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from the LORD out of the sky.
units.rightText: Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah — from the LORD out of the heavens.

units.leftText: He overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew on the ground.
units.rightText: Thus He destroyed these cities and the entire plain, including all the inhabitants of the cities and everything that grew on the ground.

units.leftText: But Lot’s wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
units.rightText: But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.

units.leftText: Abraham went up early in the morning to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
units.rightText: Early the next morning, Abraham got up and returned to the place where he had stood before the LORD.

units.leftText: He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the plain, and saw that the smoke of the land went up as the smoke of a furnace.
units.rightText: He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the land of the plain, and he saw the smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.

units.leftText: When God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the middle of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in which Lot lived.
units.rightText: So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abraham, and He brought Lot out of the catastrophe that destroyed the cities where he had lived.

units.leftText: Lot went up out of Zoar, and lived in the mountain, and his two daughters with him; for he was afraid to live in Zoar. He lived in a cave with his two daughters.
units.rightText: Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and settled in the mountains — for he was afraid to stay in Zoar — where they lived in a cave.

units.leftText: The firstborn said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is not a man on the earth to come in to us in the way of all the earth.
units.rightText: One day the older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to sleep with us, as is the custom over all the earth.

units.leftText: Come, let’s make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve our father’s family line.”
units.rightText: Come, let us get our father drunk with wine so we can sleep with him and preserve his line.”

units.leftText: They made their father drink wine that night: and the firstborn went in, and lay with her father. He didn’t know when she lay down, nor when she arose.
units.rightText: So that night they got their father drunk with wine, and the firstborn went in and slept with her father; he was not aware when she lay down or when she got up.

units.leftText: It came to pass on the next day, that the firstborn said to the younger, “Behold, I lay last night with my father. Let’s make him drink wine again tonight. You go in, and lie with him, that we may preserve our father’s family line.”
units.rightText: The next day the older daughter said to the younger, “Look, I slept with my father last night. Let us get him drunk with wine again tonight so you can go in and sleep with him and we can preserve our father’s line.”

units.leftText: They made their father drink wine that night also. The younger went and lay with him. He didn’t know when she lay down, nor when she got up.
units.rightText: So again that night they got their father drunk with wine, and the younger daughter went in and slept with him; he was not aware when she lay down or when she got up.

units.leftText: Thus both of Lot’s daughters were with child by their father.
units.rightText: Thus both of Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father.

units.leftText: The firstborn bore a son, and named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
units.rightText: The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites of today.
rightNotes: 19:37 Moab sounds like the Hebrew for from my father.

units.leftText: The younger also bore a son, and called his name Ben Ammi. He is the father of the children of Ammon to this day.
units.rightText: The younger daughter also gave birth to a son, and she named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites of today.
rightNotes: 19:38 Ben-ammi means son of my people.

units.leftText: Abraham traveled from there toward the land of the South, and lived between Kadesh and Shur. He lived as a foreigner in Gerar.
units.rightText: Now Abraham journeyed from there to the region of the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur. While he was staying in Gerar,

units.leftText: Abraham said about Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
units.rightText: Abraham said of his wife Sarah, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech king of Gerar had Sarah brought to him.

units.leftText: But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Behold, you are a dead man, because of the woman whom you have taken; for she is a man’s wife.”
units.rightText: One night, however, God came to Abimelech in a dream and told him, “You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman.”

units.leftText: Now Abimelech had not come near her. He said, “Lord, will you kill even a righteous nation?
units.rightText: Now Abimelech had not gone near her, so he replied, “Lord, would You destroy a nation even though it is innocent?

units.leftText: Didn’t he tell me, ‘She is my sister’? She, even she herself, said, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this in the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands.”
units.rightText: Didn’t Abraham tell me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this in the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands.”

units.leftText: God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I also withheld you from sinning against me. Therefore I didn’t allow you to touch her.
units.rightText: Then God said to Abimelech in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.

units.leftText: Now therefore, restore the man’s wife. For he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. If you don’t restore her, know for sure that you will die, you, and all who are yours.”
units.rightText: Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet; he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not restore her, be aware that you will surely die — you and all who belong to you.”

units.leftText: Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ear. The men were very scared.
units.rightText: Early the next morning Abimelech got up and summoned all his servants; and when he described to them all that had happened, the men were terrified.

units.leftText: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done!”
units.rightText: Then Abimelech called Abraham and asked, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought such tremendous guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done.”

units.leftText: Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see, that you have done this thing?”
units.rightText: Abimelech also asked Abraham, “What prompted you to do such a thing?”

units.leftText: Abraham said, “Because I thought, ‘Surely the fear of God is not in this place. They will kill me for my wife’s sake.’
units.rightText: Abraham replied, “I thought to myself, ‘Surely there is no fear of God in this place. They will kill me on account of my wife.’

units.leftText: Besides, she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.
units.rightText: Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father — though not the daughter of my mother — and she became my wife.

units.leftText: When God caused me to wander from my father’s house, I said to her, ‘This is your kindness which you shall show to me. Everywhere that we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
units.rightText: So when God had me journey from my father’s house, I said to Sarah, ‘This is how you can show your loyalty to me: Wherever we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”

units.leftText: Abimelech took sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored Sarah, his wife, to him.
units.rightText: So Abimelech brought sheep and cattle, menservants and maidservants, and he gave them to Abraham and restored his wife Sarah to him.

units.leftText: Abimelech said, “Behold, my land is before you. Dwell where it pleases you.”
units.rightText: And Abimelech said, “Look, my land is before you. Settle wherever you please.”

units.leftText: To Sarah he said, “Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. Behold, it is for you a covering of the eyes to all that are with you. In front of all you are vindicated.”
units.rightText: And he said to Sarah, “See, I am giving your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is your vindication before all who are with you; you are completely cleared.”
rightNotes: 20:16 Or a thousand shekels of silver; that is, approximately 25.1 pounds or 11.4 kilograms of silver

units.leftText: Abraham prayed to God. So God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, and they bore children.
units.rightText: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his maidservants, so that they could again bear children —

units.leftText: For the LORD had closed up tight all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
units.rightText: for on account of Abraham’s wife Sarah, the LORD had completely closed all the wombs in Abimelech’s household.

units.leftText: The LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did to Sarah as he had spoken.
units.rightText: Now the LORD attended to Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.

units.leftText: Sarah conceived, and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
units.rightText: So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised.

units.leftText: Abraham called his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
units.rightText: And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.
rightNotes: 21:3 Isaac means he laughs.

units.leftText: Abraham circumcised his son, Isaac, when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
units.rightText: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him.

units.leftText: Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
units.rightText: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

units.leftText: Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears will laugh with me.”
units.rightText: Then Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.”

units.leftText: She said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
units.rightText: She added, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”

units.leftText: The child grew and was weaned. Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.
units.rightText: So the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

units.leftText: Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
units.rightText: But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son,
rightNotes: 21:9 LXX and Vulgate; Hebrew lacks her son

units.leftText: Therefore she said to Abraham, “Cast out this servant and her son! For the son of this servant will not be heir with my son, Isaac.”
units.rightText: and she said to Abraham, “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!”
rightNotes: 21:10 Cited in Galatians 4:30|GAL 4:30*

units.leftText: The thing was very grievous in Abraham’s sight on account of his son.
units.rightText: Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael.

units.leftText: God said to Abraham, “Don’t let it be grievous in your sight because of the boy, and because of your servant. In all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice. For your offspring will be named through Isaac.
units.rightText: But God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.
rightNotes: 21:12 Cited in Romans 9:7|ROM 9:7* and Hebrews 11:18

units.leftText: I will also make a nation of the son of the servant, because he is your child.”
units.rightText: But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring.”

units.leftText: Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a container of water, and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder; and gave her the child, and sent her away. She departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
units.rightText: Early in the morning, Abraham got up, took bread and a skin of water, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her away with the boy. She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.

units.leftText: The water in the container was spent, and she put the child under one of the shrubs.
units.rightText: When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.

units.leftText: She went and sat down opposite him, a good way off, about a bow shot away. For she said, “Don’t let me see the death of the child.” She sat opposite him, and lifted up her voice, and wept.
units.rightText: Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away, for she said, “I cannot bear to watch the boy die!” And as she sat nearby, she lifted up her voice and wept.
rightNotes: 21:16 Hebrew; LXX the child lifted up his voice and wept

units.leftText: God heard the voice of the boy.
units.rightText: Then God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.

units.leftText: Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him with your hand. For I will make him a great nation.”
units.rightText: Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”

units.leftText: God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went, filled the container with water, and gave the boy a drink.
units.rightText: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.

units.leftText: God was with the boy, and he grew. He lived in the wilderness, and as he grew up, he became an archer.
units.rightText: And God was with the boy, and he grew up and settled in the wilderness and became a great archer.

units.leftText: He lived in the wilderness of Paran. His mother got a wife for him out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And while he was dwelling in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: At that time, Abimelech and Phicol the captain of his army spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is with you in all that you do.
units.rightText: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham, “God is with you in all that you do.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son. But according to the kindness that I have done to you, you shall do to me, and to the land in which you have lived as a foreigner.”
units.rightText: Now, therefore, swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or descendants. Show to me and to the country in which you reside the same kindness that I have shown to you.”

units.leftText: Abraham said, “I will swear.”
units.rightText: And Abraham replied, “I swear it.”

units.leftText: Abraham complained to Abimelech because of a water well, which Abimelech’s servants had violently taken away.
units.rightText: But when Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized,

units.leftText: Abimelech said, “I don’t know who has done this thing. You didn’t tell me, and I didn’t hear of it until today.”
units.rightText: Abimelech replied, “I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today.”

units.leftText: Abraham took sheep and cattle, and gave them to Abimelech. Those two made a covenant.
units.rightText: So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant.

units.leftText: Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
units.rightText: Abraham separated seven ewe lambs from the flock,

units.leftText: Abimelech said to Abraham, “What do these seven ewe lambs, which you have set by themselves, mean?”
units.rightText: and Abimelech asked him, “Why have you set apart these seven ewe lambs?”

units.leftText: He said, “You shall take these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that it may be a witness to me, that I have dug this well.”
units.rightText: He replied, “You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well.”

units.leftText: Therefore he called that place Beersheba, because they both swore an oath there.
units.rightText: So that place was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.
leftNotes: 21:31 Beersheba can mean “well of the oath” or “well of seven”.
rightNotes: 21:31 Beersheba means well of seven or well of the oath.

units.leftText: So they made a covenant at Beersheba. Abimelech rose up with Phicol, the captain of his army, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.
units.rightText: After they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.

units.leftText: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
units.rightText: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
leftNotes: 21:33 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.
rightNotes: 21:33 Hebrew El-Olam

units.leftText: Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines many days.
units.rightText: And Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for a long time.

units.leftText: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!”
units.rightText: Some time later God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!”

units.leftText: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, Isaac, whom you love, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”
units.rightText: “Take your son,” God said, “your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”

units.leftText: Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey; and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son. He split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went to the place of which God had told him.
units.rightText: So Abraham got up early the next morning, saddled his donkey, and took along two of his servants and his son Isaac. He split the wood for a burnt offering and set out for the place God had designated.

units.leftText: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place far off.
units.rightText: On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.

units.leftText: Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there. We will worship, and come back to you.”
units.rightText: “Stay here with the donkey,” Abraham told his servants. “The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will return to you.”

units.leftText: Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both went together.
units.rightText: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac. He himself carried the fire and the sacrificial knife, and the two of them walked on together.

units.leftText: Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “My father?”
units.rightText: Then Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!”

units.leftText: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.
units.rightText: Abraham answered, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” And the two walked on together.

units.leftText: They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood.
units.rightText: When they arrived at the place God had designated, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood.

units.leftText: Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.
units.rightText: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!”
units.rightText: Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven, “Abraham, Abraham!”
rightNotes: 22:11 Or Angel; also in verses 12 and 15

units.leftText: He said, “Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”
units.rightText: “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him,” said the angel, “for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me. ”
rightNotes: 22:12 Or from Me

units.leftText: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.
units.rightText: Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. So he went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
rightNotes: 22:13 Most MT manuscripts; other Hebrew manuscripts, SP, LXX, and Syriac saw one ram

units.leftText: Abraham called the name of that place “The LORD Will Provide”. As it is said to this day, “On the LORD’s mountain, it will be provided.”
units.rightText: And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. So to this day it is said, “On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.”
leftNotes: 22:14 or, the LORD Jireh, or, the LORD Seeing
rightNotes: 22:14 Hebrew YHWH Yireh

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel called to Abraham a second time out of the sky,
units.rightText: And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time,

units.leftText: and said, “‘I have sworn by myself,’ says the LORD, ‘because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son,
units.rightText: saying, “By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that because you have done this and have not withheld your only son,

units.leftText: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring will possess the gate of his enemies.
units.rightText: I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.
rightNotes: 22:17 Cited in Hebrews 6:14|HEB 6:14*

units.leftText: All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring, because you have obeyed my voice.’”
units.rightText: And through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”
rightNotes: 22:18 Cited in Acts 3:25|ACT 3:25*

units.leftText: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.
units.rightText: Abraham went back to his servants, and they got up and set out together for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba.

units.leftText: After these things, Abraham was told, “Behold, Milcah, she also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
units.rightText: Some time later, Abraham was told, “Milcah has also borne sons to your brother Nahor:

units.leftText: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
units.rightText: Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel (the father of Aram),

units.leftText: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
units.rightText: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”

units.leftText: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
units.rightText: And Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight sons to Abraham’s brother Nahor.

units.leftText: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
units.rightText: Moreover, Nahor’s concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

units.leftText: Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years. This was the length of Sarah’s life.
units.rightText: Now Sarah lived to be 127 years old.

units.leftText: Sarah died in Kiriath Arba (also called Hebron), in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
units.rightText: She died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went out to mourn and to weep for her.

units.leftText: Abraham rose up from before his dead and spoke to the children of Heth, saying,
units.rightText: Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife and said to the Hittites,
rightNotes: 23:3 Or sons of Heth; also in verses 5, 7, 10, 16, 18, and 20

units.leftText: “I am a stranger and a foreigner living with you. Give me a possession of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
units.rightText: “I am a foreigner and an outsider among you. Give me a burial site among you so that I can bury my dead.”

units.leftText: The children of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,
units.rightText: The Hittites replied to Abraham,

units.leftText: “Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. None of us will withhold from you his tomb. Bury your dead.”
units.rightText: “Listen to us, sir. You are God’s chosen one among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb for burying your dead.”

units.leftText: Abraham rose up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, to the children of Heth.
units.rightText: Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites.

units.leftText: He talked with them, saying, “If you agree that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
units.rightText: “If you are willing for me to bury my dead,” he said to them, “listen to me, and approach Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf

units.leftText: that he may sell me the cave of Machpelah, which he has, which is in the end of his field. For the full price let him sell it to me among you as a possession for a burial place.”
units.rightText: to sell me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him; it is at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me in your presence for full price, so that I may have a burial site.”

units.leftText: Now Ephron was sitting in the middle of the children of Heth. Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the children of Heth, even of all who went in at the gate of his city, saying,
units.rightText: Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth. So in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city, Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham,

units.leftText: “No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of the children of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.”
units.rightText: “No, my lord. Listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in the presence of my people. Bury your dead.”

units.leftText: Abraham bowed himself down before the people of the land.
units.rightText: Again Abraham bowed down before the people of the land

units.leftText: He spoke to Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, “But if you will, please hear me. I will give the price of the field. Take it from me, and I will bury my dead there.”
units.rightText: and said to Ephron in their presence, “If you will please listen to me, I will pay you the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there.”

units.leftText: Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
units.rightText: Ephron answered Abraham,

units.leftText: “My lord, listen to me. What is a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver between me and you? Therefore bury your dead.”
