units.rightText: “Listen to me, my lord. The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver, but what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.”
leftNotes: 23:15 A shekel is about 10 grams, so 400 shekels would be about 4 kg. or 8.8 pounds.
rightNotes: 23:15 400 shekels is approximately 10.1 pounds or 4.6 kilograms of silver; also in verse 16.

units.leftText: Abraham listened to Ephron. Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver which he had named in the hearing of the children of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, according to the current merchants’ standard.
units.rightText: Abraham agreed to Ephron’s terms and weighed out for him the price he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the standard of the merchants.

units.leftText: So the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all of its borders, were deeded
units.rightText: So Ephron’s field at Machpelah near Mamre, the cave that was in it, and all the trees within the boundaries of the field were deeded over

units.leftText: to Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all who went in at the gate of his city.
units.rightText: to Abraham’s possession in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.

units.leftText: After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (that is, Hebron), in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: The field, and the cave that is in it, were deeded to Abraham by the children of Heth as a possession for a burial place.
units.rightText: So the field and its cave were deeded by the Hittites to Abraham as a burial site.

units.leftText: Abraham was old, and well advanced in age. The LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
units.rightText: By now Abraham was old and well along in years, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.

units.leftText: Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Please put your hand under my thigh.
units.rightText: So Abraham instructed the chief servant of his household, who managed all he owned, “Place your hand under my thigh,

units.leftText: I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live.
units.rightText: and I will have you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I am dwelling,

units.leftText: But you shall go to my country, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son Isaac.”
units.rightText: but will go to my country and my kindred to take a wife for my son Isaac.”

units.leftText: The servant said to him, “What if the woman isn’t willing to follow me to this land? Must I bring your son again to the land you came from?”
units.rightText: The servant asked him, “What if the woman is unwilling to follow me to this land? Shall I then take your son back to the land from which you came?”

units.leftText: Abraham said to him, “Beware that you don’t bring my son there again.
units.rightText: Abraham replied, “Make sure that you do not take my son back there.

units.leftText: The LORD, the God of heaven—who took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to your offspring—he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
units.rightText: The LORD, the God of heaven, who brought me from my father’s house and my native land, who spoke to me and promised me on oath, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give this land’— He will send His angel before you so that you can take a wife for my son from there.

units.leftText: If the woman isn’t willing to follow you, then you shall be clear from this oath to me. Only you shall not bring my son there again.”
units.rightText: And if the woman is unwilling to follow you, then you are released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there.”

units.leftText: The servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
units.rightText: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore an oath to him concerning this matter.

units.leftText: The servant took ten of his master’s camels, and departed, having a variety of good things of his master’s with him. He arose, and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
units.rightText: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed with all manner of good things from his master in hand. And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.
rightNotes: 24:10 That is, Mesopotamia; Aram-naharaim means Aram of the two rivers, likely the region between the Euphrates and Balih Rivers in northwestern Mesopotamia.

units.leftText: He made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time that women go out to draw water.
units.rightText: As evening approached, he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town at the time when the women went out to draw water.

units.leftText: He said, “LORD, the God of my master Abraham, please give me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
units.rightText: “O LORD, God of my master Abraham,” he prayed, “please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.

units.leftText: Behold, I am standing by the spring of water. The daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.
units.rightText: Here I am, standing beside the spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water.

units.leftText: Let it happen, that the young lady to whom I will say, ‘Please let down your pitcher, that I may drink,’ then she says, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink,’—let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master.”
units.rightText: Now may it happen that the girl to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and who responds, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well’— let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. By this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.”

units.leftText: Before he had finished speaking, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher on her shoulder.
units.rightText: Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor.

units.leftText: The young lady was very beautiful to look at, a virgin. No man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
units.rightText: Now the girl was very beautiful, a virgin who had not had relations with any man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up again.

units.leftText: The servant ran to meet her, and said, “Please give me a drink, a little water from your pitcher.”
units.rightText: So the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me have a little water from your jar.”

units.leftText: She said, “Drink, my lord.” She hurried, and let down her pitcher on her hand, and gave him a drink.
units.rightText: “Drink, my lord,” she replied, and she quickly lowered her jar to her hands and gave him a drink.

units.leftText: When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will also draw for your camels, until they have finished drinking.”
units.rightText: After she had given him a drink, she said, “I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.”

units.leftText: She hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
units.rightText: And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw water, until she had drawn water for all his camels.

units.leftText: The man looked steadfastly at her, remaining silent, to know whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
units.rightText: Meanwhile, the man watched her silently to see whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.

units.leftText: As the camels had finished drinking, the man took a golden ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
units.rightText: And after the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring weighing a beka, and two gold bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels.
leftNotes: 24:22 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.
rightNotes: 24:22 A beka is half a shekel, or approximately 0.2 ounces or 5.7 grams.
24:22 10 shekels is approximately 4 ounces or 114 grams.

units.leftText: and said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to stay?”
units.rightText: “Whose daughter are you?” he asked. “Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?”

units.leftText: She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
units.rightText: She replied, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor.”

units.leftText: She said moreover to him, “We have both straw and feed enough, and room to lodge in.”
units.rightText: Then she added, “We have plenty of straw and feed, as well as a place for you to spend the night.”

units.leftText: The man bowed his head, and worshiped the LORD.
units.rightText: Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD,

units.leftText: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his loving kindness and his truth toward my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the way to the house of my master’s relatives.”
units.rightText: saying, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives.”

units.leftText: The young lady ran, and told her mother’s house about these words.
units.rightText: The girl ran and told her mother’s household about these things.

units.leftText: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.
units.rightText: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he rushed out to the man at the spring.

units.leftText: When he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man. Behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
units.rightText: As soon as he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and heard Rebekah’s words, “The man said this to me,” he went and found the man standing by the camels near the spring.

units.leftText: He said, “Come in, you blessed of the LORD. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.”
units.rightText: “Come, you who are blessed by the LORD,” said Laban. “Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”

units.leftText: The man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels. He gave straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
units.rightText: So the man came to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and feed were brought to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of his companions.

units.leftText: Food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told my message.”
units.rightText: Then a meal was set before the man, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told you what I came to say.”

units.leftText: He said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
units.rightText: “I am Abraham’s servant,” he replied.

units.leftText: The LORD has blessed my master greatly. He has become great. The LORD has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
units.rightText: “The LORD has greatly blessed my master, and he has become rich. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, menservants and maidservants, camels and donkeys.

units.leftText: Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.
units.rightText: My master’s wife Sarah has borne him a son in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns.

units.leftText: My master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
units.rightText: My master made me swear an oath and said, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I dwell,

units.leftText: but you shall go to my father’s house, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son.’
units.rightText: but you shall go to my father’s house and to my kindred to take a wife for my son.’

units.leftText: I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not follow me?’
units.rightText: Then I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not come back with me?’

units.leftText: He said to me, ‘The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and prosper your way. You shall take a wife for my son from my relatives, and of my father’s house.
units.rightText: And he told me, ‘The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you may take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father’s house.

units.leftText: Then you will be clear from my oath, when you come to my relatives. If they don’t give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.’
units.rightText: And when you go to my kindred, if they refuse to give her to you, then you will be released from my oath.’

units.leftText: I came today to the spring, and said, ‘The LORD, the God of my master Abraham, if now you do prosper my way which I go—
units.rightText: So when I came to the spring today, I prayed: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if only You would make my journey a success!

units.leftText: behold, I am standing by this spring of water. Let it happen, that the maiden who comes out to draw, to whom I will say, “Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,”
units.rightText: Here I am, standing beside this spring. Now if a maiden comes out to draw water and I say to her, ‘Please let me drink a little water from your jar,’

units.leftText: then she tells me, “Drink, and I will also draw for your camels,”—let her be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.’
units.rightText: and she replies, ‘Drink, and I will draw water for your camels as well,’ may she be the woman the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.

units.leftText: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder. She went down to the spring, and drew. I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’
units.rightText: And before I had finished praying in my heart, there was Rebekah coming out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. So I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’

units.leftText: She hurried and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels a drink.
units.rightText: She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well.’ So I drank, and she also watered the camels.

units.leftText: I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands.
units.rightText: Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’

units.leftText: I bowed my head, and worshiped the LORD, and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
units.rightText: Then I bowed down and worshiped the LORD; and I blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to take the granddaughter of my master’s brother for his son.

units.leftText: Now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. If not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.”
units.rightText: Now if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; but if not, let me know, so that I may go elsewhere.”

units.leftText: Then Laban and Bethuel answered, “The thing proceeds from the LORD. We can’t speak to you bad or good.
units.rightText: Laban and Bethuel answered, “This is from the LORD; we have no choice in the matter.

units.leftText: Behold, Rebekah is before you. Take her, and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as the LORD has spoken.”
units.rightText: Rebekah is here before you. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, just as the LORD has decreed.”

units.leftText: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself down to the earth to the LORD.
units.rightText: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.

units.leftText: The servant brought out jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and her mother.
units.rightText: Then he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and he gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother.

units.leftText: They ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and stayed all night. They rose up in the morning, and he said, “Send me away to my master.”
units.rightText: Then he and the men with him ate and drank and spent the night there.

units.leftText: Her brother and her mother said, “Let the young lady stay with us a few days, at least ten. After that she will go.”
units.rightText: But her brother and mother said, “Let the girl remain with us ten days or so. After that, she may go.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Don’t hinder me, since the LORD has prospered my way. Send me away that I may go to my master.”
units.rightText: But he replied, “Do not delay me, since the LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so that I may go to my master.”

units.leftText: They said, “We will call the young lady, and ask her.”
units.rightText: So they said, “We will call the girl and ask her opinion.”

units.leftText: They called Rebekah, and said to her, “Will you go with this man?”
units.rightText: They called Rebekah and asked her, “Will you go with this man?”

units.leftText: They sent away Rebekah, their sister, with her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his men.
units.rightText: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.

units.leftText: They blessed Rebekah, and said to her, “Our sister, may you be the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let your offspring possess the gate of those who hate them.”
units.rightText: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her,

units.leftText: Rebekah arose with her ladies. They rode on the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
units.rightText: Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.

units.leftText: Isaac came from the way of Beer Lahai Roi, for he lived in the land of the South.
units.rightText: Now Isaac had just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, for he was living in the Negev.

units.leftText: Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the evening. He lifted up his eyes and looked. Behold, there were camels coming.
units.rightText: Early in the evening, Isaac went out to the field to meditate, and looking up, he saw the camels approaching.

units.leftText: Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she got off the camel.

units.rightText: So now, my son, obey my voice and flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.

units.leftText: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury turns away—
units.rightText: Stay with him for a while, until your brother’s fury subsides—

units.leftText: until your brother’s anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send, and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”
units.rightText: until your brother’s rage against you wanes and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”

units.leftText: Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?”
units.rightText: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?”
rightNotes: 27:46 Or daughters of Heth

units.leftText: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and commanded him, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
units.rightText: So Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him. “Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women,” he commanded.

units.leftText: Arise, go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father. Take a wife from there from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
units.rightText: “Go at once to Paddan-aram, to the house of your mother’s father Bethuel, and take a wife from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
rightNotes: 28:2 That is, northwest Mesopotamia; also in verses 5, 6, and 7

units.leftText: May God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a company of peoples,
units.rightText: May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you may become a company of peoples.
rightNotes: 28:3 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: and give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, that you may inherit the land where you travel, which God gave to Abraham.”
units.rightText: And may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants, so that you may possess the land where you dwell as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham.”

units.leftText: Isaac sent Jacob away. He went to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.
units.rightText: So Isaac sent Jacob to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, who was the mother of Jacob and Esau.

units.leftText: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan Aram, to take him a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;”
units.rightText: Now Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to take a wife there, commanding him, “Do not marry a Canaanite woman,”

units.leftText: and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan Aram.
units.rightText: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.

units.leftText: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan didn’t please Isaac, his father.
units.rightText: And seeing that his father Isaac disapproved of the Canaanite women,

units.leftText: So Esau went to Ishmael, and took, in addition to the wives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his wife.
units.rightText: Esau went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Abraham’s son Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had.

units.leftText: Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.
units.rightText: Meanwhile Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.

units.leftText: He came to a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun had set. He took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.
units.rightText: On reaching a certain place, he spent the night there because the sun had set. And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.

units.leftText: He dreamed and saw a stairway set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven. Behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
units.rightText: And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.

units.leftText: Behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. I will give the land you lie on to you and to your offspring.
units.rightText: And there at the top the LORD was standing and saying, “I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you now lie.
rightNotes: 28:13 Or there beside him

units.leftText: Your offspring will be as the dust of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in your offspring, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
units.rightText: Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and east and north and south. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.

units.leftText: Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.”
units.rightText: Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”

units.leftText: Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
units.rightText: When Jacob woke up, he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.”

units.leftText: He was afraid, and said, “How awesome this place is! This is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven.”
units.rightText: And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven!”

units.leftText: Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil on its top.
units.rightText: Early the next morning, Jacob took the stone that he had placed under his head, and he set it up as a pillar. He poured oil on top of it,

units.leftText: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.
units.rightText: and he called that place Bethel, though previously the city had been named Luz.
rightNotes: 28:19 Bethel means house of God.

units.leftText: Jacob vowed a vow, saying, “If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and clothing to put on,
units.rightText: Then Jacob made a vow, saying, “If God will be with me and watch over me on this journey, and if He will provide me with food to eat and clothes to wear,

units.leftText: so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, and the LORD will be my God,
units.rightText: so that I may return safely to my father’s house, then the LORD will be my God.

units.leftText: then this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, will be God’s house. Of all that you will give me I will surely give a tenth to you.”
units.rightText: And this stone I have set up as a pillar will be God’s house, and of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth.”

units.leftText: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.
units.rightText: Jacob resumed his journey and came to the land of the people of the east.

units.leftText: He looked, and saw a well in the field, and saw three flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that well they watered the flocks. The stone on the well’s mouth was large.
units.rightText: He looked and saw a well in the field, and near it lay three flocks of sheep, because the sheep were watered from this well. And a large stone covered the mouth of the well.

units.leftText: There all the flocks were gathered. They rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone back on the well’s mouth in its place.
units.rightText: When all the flocks had been gathered there, the shepherds would roll away the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.

units.leftText: Jacob said to them, “My relatives, where are you from?”
units.rightText: “My brothers,” Jacob asked the shepherds, “where are you from?”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?”
units.rightText: “Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor?” Jacob asked.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Is it well with him?”
units.rightText: “Is he well?” Jacob inquired.

units.leftText: He said, “Behold, it is still the middle of the day, not time to gather the livestock together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.”
units.rightText: “Look,” said Jacob, “it is still broad daylight; it is not yet time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture.”

units.leftText: They said, “We can’t, until all the flocks are gathered together, and they roll the stone from the well’s mouth. Then we will water the sheep.”
units.rightText: But they replied, “We cannot, until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will water the sheep.”

units.leftText: While he was yet speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she kept them.
units.rightText: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

units.leftText: When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
units.rightText: As soon as Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, with Laban’s sheep, he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.

units.leftText: Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
units.rightText: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and wept aloud.

units.leftText: Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s relative, and that he was Rebekah’s son. She ran and told her father.
units.rightText: He told Rachel that he was Rebekah’s son, a relative of her father, and she ran and told her father.

units.leftText: When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.
units.rightText: When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him all that had happened.

units.leftText: Laban said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.” Jacob stayed with him for a month.
units.rightText: Then Laban declared, “You are indeed my own flesh and blood.”

units.leftText: Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what will your wages be?”
units.rightText: Laban said to him, “Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”

units.leftText: Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
units.rightText: Now Laban had two daughters; the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.

units.leftText: Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.
units.rightText: Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.
rightNotes: 29:17 Or had delicate eyes

units.leftText: Jacob loved Rachel. He said, “I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.”
units.rightText: Since Jacob loved Rachel, he answered, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”

units.leftText: Laban said, “It is better that I give her to you, than that I should give her to another man. Stay with me.”
units.rightText: Laban replied, “Better that I give her to you than to another. Stay here with me.”

units.leftText: Jacob served seven years for Rachel. They seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.
units.rightText: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.

units.leftText: Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
units.rightText: Finally Jacob said to Laban, “Grant me my wife, for my time is complete, and I want to sleep with her.”

units.leftText: Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
units.rightText: So Laban invited all the men of that place and prepared a feast.

units.leftText: In the evening, he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to Jacob. He went in to her.
units.rightText: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and he slept with her.

units.leftText: Laban gave Zilpah his servant to his daughter Leah for a servant.
units.rightText: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.

units.leftText: In the morning, behold, it was Leah! He said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Didn’t I serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?”
units.rightText: When morning came, there was Leah! “What have you done to me?” Jacob said to Laban. “Wasn’t it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?”

units.leftText: Laban said, “It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
units.rightText: Laban replied, “It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.

units.leftText: Fulfill the week of this one, and we will give you the other also for the service which you will serve with me for seven more years.”
units.rightText: Finish this week’s celebration, and we will give you the younger one in return for another seven years of work.”

units.leftText: Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week. He gave him Rachel his daughter as wife.
units.rightText: And Jacob did just that. He finished the week’s celebration, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.

units.leftText: Laban gave Bilhah, his servant, to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.
units.rightText: Laban also gave his servant girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maidservant.

units.leftText: He went in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him seven more years.
units.rightText: Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and indeed, he loved Rachel more than Leah. So he worked for Laban another seven years.

units.leftText: The LORD saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
units.rightText: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.

units.leftText: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “Because the LORD has looked at my affliction; for now my husband will love me.”
units.rightText: And Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.”
rightNotes: 29:32 Reuben means Look, a son and also sounds like the Hebrew for He has seen my misery.

units.leftText: She conceived again, and bore a son, and said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon.
units.rightText: Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son as well.” So she named him Simeon.
rightNotes: 29:33 Simeon probably means one who hears.

units.leftText: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Levi.
units.rightText: Once again Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So he was named Levi.
rightNotes: 29:34 Levi sounds like the Hebrew for being attached to or feeling affection for.

units.leftText: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.
units.rightText: And once more she conceived and gave birth to a son and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” So she named him Judah. Then Leah stopped having children.
rightNotes: 29:35 Judah sounds like the Hebrew for praise.

units.leftText: When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. She said to Jacob, “Give me children, or else I will die.”
units.rightText: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing any children for Jacob, she envied her sister. “Give me children, or I will die!” she said to Jacob.

units.leftText: Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel, and he said, “Am I in God’s place, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?”
units.rightText: Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?”

units.leftText: She said, “Behold, my maid Bilhah. Go in to her, that she may bear on my knees, and I also may obtain children by her.”
units.rightText: Then she said, “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.”
rightNotes: 30:3 Literally bear children on my knees

units.leftText: She gave him Bilhah her servant as wife, and Jacob went in to her.
units.rightText: So Rachel gave Jacob her servant Bilhah as a wife, and he slept with her,

units.leftText: Bilhah conceived, and bore Jacob a son.
units.rightText: and Bilhah conceived and bore him a son.

units.leftText: Rachel said, “God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan.
units.rightText: Then Rachel said, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.” So she named him Dan.
rightNotes: 30:6 Dan means He has judged or He has vindicated.

units.leftText: Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son.
units.rightText: And Rachel’s servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

units.leftText: Rachel said, “I have wrestled with my sister with mighty wrestlings, and have prevailed.” She named him Naphtali.
units.rightText: Then Rachel said, “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.” So she named him Naphtali.
rightNotes: 30:8 Naphtali sounds like the Hebrew for wrestling.

units.leftText: When Leah saw that she had finished bearing, she took Zilpah, her servant, and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
units.rightText: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.

units.leftText: Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a son.
units.rightText: And Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.

units.leftText: Leah said, “How fortunate!” She named him Gad.
units.rightText: Then Leah said, “How fortunate!” So she named him Gad.
rightNotes: 30:11 Alternate MT reading (see also LXX); the other alternate reads “A troop is coming!”
30:11 Gad sounds like the Hebrew for good fortune, or alternately for band of raiders.

units.leftText: Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a second son.
units.rightText: When Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son,

units.leftText: Leah said, “Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.” She named him Asher.
units.rightText: Leah said, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” So she named him Asher.
rightNotes: 30:13 Asher means happy.

units.leftText: Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother, Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
units.rightText: Now during the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found some mandrakes in the field. When he brought them to his mother, Rachel begged Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

units.leftText: Leah said to her, “Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? Would you take away my son’s mandrakes, also?”
units.rightText: But Leah replied, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband? Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes as well?”

units.leftText: Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, “You must come in to me; for I have surely hired you with my son’s mandrakes.”
units.rightText: When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, “You must come with me, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night.

units.leftText: God listened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son.
units.rightText: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.

units.leftText: Leah said, “God has given me my hire, because I gave my servant to my husband.” She named him Issachar.
units.rightText: Then Leah said, “God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband.” So she named him Issachar.
rightNotes: 30:18 Issachar sounds like the Hebrew for wages or reward.

units.leftText: Leah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
units.rightText: Again Leah conceived and bore a sixth son to Jacob.

units.leftText: Leah said, “God has endowed me with a good dowry. Now my husband will live with me, because I have borne him six sons.” She named him Zebulun.
units.rightText: “God has given me a good gift,” she said. “This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.” And she named him Zebulun.
rightNotes: 30:20 Zebulun sounds like the Hebrew for honor.

units.leftText: Afterwards, she bore a daughter, and named her Dinah.
units.rightText: After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah.

units.leftText: God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her, and opened her womb.
units.rightText: Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb,

units.leftText: She conceived, bore a son, and said, “God has taken away my reproach.”
units.rightText: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. “God has taken away my shame,” she said.

units.leftText: She named him Joseph, saying, “May the LORD add another son to me.”
units.rightText: She named him Joseph, and said, “May the LORD add to me another son.”
rightNotes: 30:24 Joseph means may He add.

units.leftText: When Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away, that I may go to my own place, and to my country.
units.rightText: Now after Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me on my way so I can return to my homeland.

units.leftText: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you know my service with which I have served you.”
units.rightText: Give me my wives and children for whom I have served you, that I may go on my way. You know how hard I have worked for you.”

units.leftText: Laban said to him, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, stay here, for I have divined that the LORD has blessed me for your sake.”
units.rightText: But Laban replied, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay. I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you.”

units.leftText: He said, “Appoint me your wages, and I will give it.”
units.rightText: And he added, “Name your wages, and I will pay them.”

units.leftText: Jacob said to him, “You know how I have served you, and how your livestock have fared with me.
units.rightText: Then Jacob answered, “You know how I have served you and how your livestock have thrived under my care.

units.leftText: For it was little which you had before I came, and it has increased to a multitude. The LORD has blessed you wherever I turned. Now when will I provide for my own house also?”
units.rightText: Indeed, you had very little before my arrival, but now your wealth has increased many times over. The LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot. But now, when may I also provide for my own household?”

units.leftText: Laban said, “What shall I give you?”
units.rightText: “What can I give you?” Laban asked.

units.leftText: I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This will be my hire.
units.rightText: Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. These will be my wages.

units.leftText: So my righteousness will answer for me hereafter, when you come concerning my hire that is before you. Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that might be with me, will be considered stolen.”
units.rightText: So my honesty will testify for me when you come to check on my wages in the future. If I have any goats that are not speckled or spotted, or any lambs that are not dark-colored, they will be considered stolen.”

units.leftText: Laban said, “Behold, let it be according to your word.”
units.rightText: “Agreed,” said Laban. “Let it be as you have said.”

units.leftText: That day, he removed the male goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
units.rightText: That very day Laban removed all the streaked or spotted male goats and every speckled or spotted female goat— every one that had any white on it— and every dark-colored lamb, and he placed them under the care of his sons.

units.leftText: He set three days’ journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.
units.rightText: Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob was shepherding the rest of Laban’s flocks.

units.leftText: Jacob took to himself rods of fresh poplar, almond, and plane tree, peeled white streaks in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
units.rightText: Jacob, however, took fresh branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled the bark, exposing the white inner wood of the branches.

units.leftText: He set the rods which he had peeled opposite the flocks in the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink. They conceived when they came to drink.
units.rightText: Then he set the peeled branches in the watering troughs in front of the flocks coming in to drink. So when the flocks were in heat and came to drink,

units.leftText: The flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks produced streaked, speckled, and spotted.
units.rightText: they mated in front of the branches. And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.

units.leftText: Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the streaked and all the black in Laban’s flock. He put his own droves apart, and didn’t put them into Laban’s flock.
units.rightText: Jacob set apart the young, but made the rest face the streaked dark-colored sheep in Laban’s flocks. Then he set his own stock apart and did not put them with Laban’s animals.

units.leftText: Whenever the stronger of the flock conceived, Jacob laid the rods in front of the eyes of the flock in the watering troughs, that they might conceive among the rods;
units.rightText: Whenever the stronger females of the flock were in heat, Jacob would place the branches in the troughs, in full view of the animals, so that they would breed in front of the branches.

units.leftText: but when the flock were feeble, he didn’t put them in. So the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.
units.rightText: But if the animals were weak, he did not set out the branches. So the weaker animals went to Laban and the stronger ones to Jacob.

units.leftText: The man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, female servants and male servants, and camels and donkeys.
units.rightText: Thus Jacob became exceedingly prosperous. He owned large flocks, maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.

units.leftText: Jacob heard Laban’s sons’ words, saying, “Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s. He has obtained all this wealth from that which was our father’s.”
units.rightText: Now Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”

units.leftText: Jacob saw the expression on Laban’s face, and, behold, it was not toward him as before.
units.rightText: And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your fathers, and to your relatives, and I will be with you.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”

units.leftText: Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field to his flock,
units.rightText: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were,

units.leftText: and said to them, “I see the expression on your father’s face, that it is not toward me as before; but the God of my father has been with me.
units.rightText: and he told them, “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.

units.leftText: You know that I have served your father with all of my strength.
units.rightText: You know that I have served your father with all my strength.

units.leftText: Your father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, but God didn’t allow him to hurt me.
units.rightText: And although he has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, God has not allowed him to harm me.

units.leftText: If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked.
units.rightText: If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore speckled offspring. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore streaked offspring.

units.leftText: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock, and given them to me.
units.rightText: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.

units.leftText: During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats which leaped on the flock were streaked, speckled, and grizzled.
units.rightText: When the flocks were breeding, I saw in a dream that the streaked, spotted, and speckled males were mating with the females.

units.leftText: The angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob,’ and I said, ‘Here I am.’
units.rightText: In that dream the angel of God said to me, ‘Jacob!’
rightNotes: 31:11 Or Angel

units.leftText: He said, ‘Now lift up your eyes, and behold, all the male goats which leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.
units.rightText: ‘Look up,’ he said, ‘and see that all the males that are mating with the flock are streaked, spotted, or speckled; for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.

units.leftText: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar, where you vowed a vow to me. Now arise, get out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.’”
units.rightText: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me. Now get up, leave this land at once, and return to your native land.’”

units.leftText: Rachel and Leah answered him, “Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?
units.rightText: And Rachel and Leah replied, “Do we have any portion or inheritance left in our father’s house?

units.leftText: Aren’t we considered as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also used up our money.
units.rightText: Are we not regarded by him as outsiders? Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.

units.leftText: For all the riches which God has taken away from our father are ours and our children’s. Now then, whatever God has said to you, do.”
units.rightText: Surely all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. So do whatever God has told you.”

units.leftText: Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives on the camels,
units.rightText: Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on camels,

units.leftText: and he took away all his livestock, and all his possessions which he had gathered, including the livestock which he had gained in Paddan Aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: and he drove all his livestock before him, along with all the possessions he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.
rightNotes: 31:18 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole the teraphim that were her father’s.
units.rightText: Now while Laban was out shearing his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household idols.
leftNotes: 31:19 teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property.

units.leftText: Jacob deceived Laban the Syrian, in that he didn’t tell him that he was running away.
units.rightText: Moreover, Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.
rightNotes: 31:20 Or stole the heart of; also in verses 26 and 27

units.leftText: So he fled with all that he had. He rose up, passed over the River, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.
units.rightText: So he fled with all his possessions, crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.
rightNotes: 31:21 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: Laban was told on the third day that Jacob had fled.
units.rightText: On the third day Laban was informed that Jacob had fled.

units.leftText: He took his relatives with him, and pursued him seven days’ journey. He overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.
units.rightText: So he took his relatives with him, pursued Jacob for seven days, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.

units.leftText: God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.”
units.rightText: But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and warned him, “Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.”

units.leftText: Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.
units.rightText: Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there as well.

units.leftText: Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done, that you have deceived me, and carried away my daughters like captives of the sword?
units.rightText: Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives of war!

units.leftText: Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn’t tell me, that I might have sent you away with mirth and with songs, with tambourine and with harp;
units.rightText: Why did you run away secretly and deceive me, without even telling me? I would have sent you away with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.

units.leftText: and didn’t allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters? Now you have done foolishly.
units.rightText: But you did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. Now you have done a foolish thing.

units.leftText: It is in the power of my hand to hurt you, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, ‘Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.’
units.rightText: I have power to do you great harm, but last night the God of your father said to me, ‘Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.’

units.leftText: Now, you want to be gone, because you greatly longed for your father’s house, but why have you stolen my gods?”
units.rightText: Now you have gone off because you long for your father’s house. But why have you stolen my gods?”

units.leftText: Jacob answered Laban, “Because I was afraid, for I said, ‘Lest you should take your daughters from me by force.’
units.rightText: “I was afraid,” Jacob answered, “for I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.

units.leftText: Anyone you find your gods with shall not live. Before our relatives, discern what is yours with me, and take it.” For Jacob didn’t know that Rachel had stolen them.
units.rightText: If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live! In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself if anything is yours, and take it back.” For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.

units.leftText: Laban went into Jacob’s tent, into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two female servants; but he didn’t find them. He went out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.
units.rightText: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, then Leah’s tent, and then the tents of the two maidservants, but he found nothing. Then he left Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.

units.leftText: Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find them.
units.rightText: Now Rachel had taken Laban’s household idols, put them in the saddlebag of her camel, and was sitting on them. And Laban searched everything in the tent but found nothing.

units.leftText: She said to her father, “Don’t let my lord be angry that I can’t rise up before you; for I’m having my period.” He searched, but didn’t find the teraphim.
units.rightText: Rachel said to her father, “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.” So Laban searched but could not find the household idols.

units.leftText: Jacob was angry, and argued with Laban. Jacob answered Laban, “What is my trespass? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?
units.rightText: Then Jacob became incensed and challenged Laban. “What is my crime?” he said. “For what sin of mine have you so hotly pursued me?

units.leftText: Now that you have felt around in all my stuff, what have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge between us two.
units.rightText: You have searched all my goods! Have you found anything that belongs to you? Put it here before my brothers and yours, that they may judge between the two of us.

units.leftText: “These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not cast their young, and I haven’t eaten the rams of your flocks.
units.rightText: I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flock.

units.leftText: That which was torn of animals, I didn’t bring to you. I bore its loss. Of my hand you required it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.
units.rightText: I did not bring you anything torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for what was stolen by day or night.

units.leftText: This was my situation: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes.
units.rightText: As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.

units.leftText: These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.
units.rightText: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household— fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks— and you have changed my wages ten times!

units.leftText: Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”
units.rightText: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, surely by now you would have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and last night He rendered judgment.”

units.leftText: Laban answered Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine! What can I do today to these my daughters, or to their children whom they have borne?
units.rightText: But Laban answered Jacob, “These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks! Everything you see is mine! Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine or the children they have borne?

units.leftText: Now come, let’s make a covenant, you and I. Let it be for a witness between me and you.”
units.rightText: Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”

units.leftText: Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
units.rightText: So Jacob picked out a stone and set it up as a pillar,

units.leftText: Jacob said to his relatives, “Gather stones.” They took stones, and made a heap. They ate there by the heap.
units.rightText: and he said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and made a mound, and there by the mound they ate.

units.leftText: Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, but Jacob called it Galeed.
units.rightText: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
rightNotes: 31:47 The Aramaic Jegar-sahadutha and the Hebrew Galeed both mean heap of witnesses.

units.leftText: Laban said, “This heap is witness between me and you today.” Therefore it was named Galeed
units.rightText: Then Laban declared, “This mound is a witness between you and me this day.”

units.leftText: and Mizpah, for he said, “The LORD watch between me and you, when we are absent one from another.
units.rightText: It was also called Mizpah, because Laban said, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.
rightNotes: 31:49 Mizpah means watchtower.

units.leftText: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives in addition to my daughters, no man is with us; behold, God is witness between me and you.”
units.rightText: If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, although no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”

units.leftText: Laban said to Jacob, “See this heap, and see the pillar, which I have set between me and you.
units.rightText: Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is the mound, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.

units.leftText: May this heap be a witness, and the pillar be a witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and that you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.
units.rightText: This mound is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.

units.leftText: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” Then Jacob swore by the fear of his father, Isaac.
units.rightText: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.”

units.leftText: Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his relatives to eat bread. They ate bread, and stayed all night in the mountain.
units.rightText: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. And after they had eaten, they spent the night on the mountain.

units.leftText: Early in the morning, Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Laban departed and returned to his place.
units.rightText: Early the next morning, Laban got up and kissed his grandchildren and daughters and blessed them. Then he left to return home.

units.leftText: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
units.rightText: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

units.leftText: When he saw them, Jacob said, “This is God’s army.” He called the name of that place Mahanaim.
units.rightText: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.” So he named that place Mahanaim.
rightNotes: 32:2 Mahanaim means two camps.

units.leftText: Jacob sent messengers in front of him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
units.rightText: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

units.leftText: He commanded them, saying, “This is what you shall tell my lord, Esau: ‘This is what your servant, Jacob, says. I have lived as a foreigner with Laban, and stayed until now.
units.rightText: He instructed them, “You are to say to my master Esau, ‘Your servant Jacob says: I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.

units.leftText: I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in your sight.’”
units.rightText: I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants, and maidservants. I have sent this message to inform my master, so that I may find favor in your sight.’”

units.leftText: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau. He is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”
units.rightText: When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you— he and four hundred men with him.”

units.leftText: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and was distressed. He divided the people who were with him, along with the flocks, the herds, and the camels, into two companies.
units.rightText: In great fear and distress, Jacob divided his people into two camps, as well as the flocks and herds and camels.

units.leftText: He said, “If Esau comes to the one company, and strikes it, then the company which is left will escape.”
units.rightText: He thought, “If Esau comes and attacks one camp, then the other camp can escape.”

units.leftText: Jacob said, “God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, the LORD, who said to me, ‘Return to your country, and to your relatives, and I will do you good,’
units.rightText: Then Jacob declared, “O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, the LORD who told me, ‘Go back to your country and to your kindred, and I will make you prosper,’

units.leftText: I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your servant; for with just my staff I crossed over this Jordan; and now I have become two companies.
units.rightText: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. Indeed, with only my staff I came across the Jordan, but now I have become two camps.

units.leftText: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and strike me and the mothers with the children.
units.rightText: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid that he may come and attack me and the mothers and children with me.

units.leftText: You said, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your offspring as the sand of the sea, which can’t be counted because there are so many.’”
units.rightText: But You have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’”

units.leftText: He stayed there that night, and took from that which he had with him a present for Esau, his brother:
units.rightText: Jacob spent the night there, and from what he had brought with him, he selected a gift for his brother Esau:

units.leftText: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
units.rightText: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams,

units.leftText: thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.
units.rightText: 30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.

units.leftText: He delivered them into the hands of his servants, every herd by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put a space between herd and herd.”
units.rightText: He entrusted them to his servants in separate herds and told them, “Go on ahead of me, and keep some distance between the herds.”

units.leftText: He commanded the foremost, saying, “When Esau, my brother, meets you, and asks you, saying, ‘Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these before you?’
units.rightText: He instructed the one in the lead, “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘To whom do you belong, where are you going, and whose animals are these before you?’

units.leftText: Then you shall say, ‘They are your servant, Jacob’s. It is a present sent to my lord, Esau. Behold, he also is behind us.’”
units.rightText: then you are to say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift, sent to my lord Esau. And behold, Jacob is behind us.’”

units.leftText: He commanded also the second, and the third, and all that followed the herds, saying, “This is how you shall speak to Esau, when you find him.
units.rightText: He also instructed the second, the third, and all those following behind the herds: “When you meet Esau, you are to say the same thing to him.

units.leftText: You shall say, ‘Not only that, but behold, your servant, Jacob, is behind us.’” For, he said, “I will appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face. Perhaps he will accept me.”
units.rightText: You are also to say, ‘Look, your servant Jacob is right behind us.’” For he thought, “I will appease Esau with the gift that is going before me. After that I can face him, and perhaps he will accept me. ”
rightNotes: 32:20 Or I will appease his face
32:20 Literally perhaps he will lift up my face

units.leftText: So the present passed over before him, and he himself stayed that night in the camp.
units.rightText: So Jacob’s gifts went on before him, while he spent the night in the camp.

units.leftText: He rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two servants, and his eleven sons, and crossed over the ford of the Jabbok.
units.rightText: During the night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

units.leftText: He took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that which he had.
units.rightText: He took them and sent them across the stream, along with all his possessions.

units.leftText: Jacob was left alone, and wrestled with a man there until the breaking of the day.
units.rightText: So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
rightNotes: 32:24 Or Man; here and in verses 25–28; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized

units.leftText: When he saw that he didn’t prevail against him, the man touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained as he wrestled.
units.rightText: When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.

units.leftText: The man said, “Let me go, for the day breaks.”
units.rightText: Then the man said, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.”

units.leftText: He said to him, “What is your name?”
units.rightText: “What is your name?” the man asked.

units.leftText: He said, “Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed.”
units.rightText: Then the man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.”
rightNotes: 32:28 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.
32:28 Israel means he struggles with God.

units.leftText: Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.”
units.rightText: And Jacob requested, “Please tell me your name.”

units.leftText: Jacob called the name of the place Peniel; for he said, “I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”
units.rightText: So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”
rightNotes: 32:30 Peniel means the face of God.

units.leftText: The sun rose on him as he passed over Peniel, and he limped because of his thigh.
units.rightText: The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
rightNotes: 32:31 Penuel is a variant of Peniel; see verse 30.

units.leftText: Therefore the children of Israel don’t eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.
units.rightText: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.

units.leftText: Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children between Leah, Rachel, and the two servants.
units.rightText: Now Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming toward him with four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants.

units.leftText: He put the servants and their children in front, Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.
units.rightText: He put the maidservants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.

units.leftText: He himself passed over in front of them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
units.rightText: But Jacob himself went on ahead and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.

units.leftText: Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.
units.rightText: Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him. And they both wept.

units.leftText: He lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, “Who are these with you?”
units.rightText: When Esau looked up and saw the women and children, he asked, “Who are these with you?”

units.leftText: Then the servants came near with their children, and they bowed themselves.
units.rightText: Then the maidservants and their children approached and bowed down.

units.leftText: Leah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves. After them, Joseph came near with Rachel, and they bowed themselves.
units.rightText: Leah and her children also approached and bowed down, and then Joseph and Rachel approached and bowed down.

units.leftText: Esau said, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?”
units.rightText: “What do you mean by sending this whole company to meet me?” asked Esau.

units.leftText: Esau said, “I have enough, my brother; let that which you have be yours.”
units.rightText: “I already have plenty, my brother,” Esau replied. “Keep what belongs to you.”

units.leftText: Jacob said, “Please, no, if I have now found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me.
units.rightText: But Jacob insisted, “No, please! If I have found favor in your sight, then receive this gift from my hand. For indeed, I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.

units.leftText: Please take the gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he took it.
units.rightText: Please accept my gift that was brought to you, because God has been gracious to me and I have all I need.” So Jacob pressed him until he accepted.
rightNotes: 33:11 Or blessing or treaty of peace

units.leftText: Esau said, “Let’s take our journey, and let’s go, and I will go before you.”
units.rightText: Then Esau said, “Let us be on our way, and I will go ahead of you.”

units.leftText: Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.
units.rightText: But Jacob replied, “My lord knows that the children are frail, and I must care for sheep and cattle that are nursing their young. If they are driven hard for even a day, all the animals will die.

units.leftText: Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir.”
units.rightText: Please let my lord go ahead of his servant. I will continue on slowly, at a comfortable pace for the livestock and children, until I come to my lord at Seir.”

units.leftText: Esau said, “Let me now leave with you some of the people who are with me.”
units.rightText: “Let me leave some of my people with you,” Esau said.

units.leftText: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
units.rightText: So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir,

units.leftText: Jacob traveled to Succoth, built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.
units.rightText: but Jacob went on to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and shelters for his livestock; that is why the place was called Succoth.
rightNotes: 33:17 Succoth means booths or shelters or tabernacles; twice in this verse.

units.leftText: Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan Aram; and encamped before the city.
units.rightText: After Jacob had come from Paddan-aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, and he camped just outside the city.
rightNotes: 33:18 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.
units.rightText: And the plot of ground where he pitched his tent, he purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver.
rightNotes: 33:19 Hebrew a hundred kesitahs; the value or weight of the kesitah is no longer known

units.leftText: He erected an altar there, and called it El Elohe Israel.
units.rightText: There he set up an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
leftNotes: 33:20 El Elohe Israel means “God, the God of Israel” or “The God of Israel is mighty”.
rightNotes: 33:20 El-Elohe-Israel means God is the God of Israel or mighty is the God of Israel.
