units.leftText: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
units.rightText: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the daughters of the land.

units.leftText: Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her, lay with her, and humbled her.
units.rightText: When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the region, saw her, he took her and lay with her by force.

units.leftText: His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.
units.rightText: And his soul was drawn to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. He loved the young girl and spoke to her tenderly.

units.leftText: Shechem spoke to his father, Hamor, saying, “Get me this young lady as a wife.”
units.rightText: So Shechem told his father Hamor, “Get me this girl as a wife.”

units.leftText: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah, his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field. Jacob held his peace until they came.
units.rightText: Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah, but since his sons were with his livestock in the field, he remained silent about it until they returned.

units.leftText: Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to talk with him.
units.rightText: Meanwhile, Shechem’s father Hamor came to speak with Jacob.

units.leftText: The sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it. The men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter, a thing that ought not to be done.
units.rightText: When Jacob’s sons heard what had happened, they returned from the field. They were filled with grief and fury, because Shechem had committed an outrage in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter — a thing that should not be done.
rightNotes: 34:7 Or against Israel

units.leftText: Hamor talked with them, saying, “The soul of my son, Shechem, longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
units.rightText: But Hamor said to them, “My son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.

units.leftText: Make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
units.rightText: Intermarry with us; give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves.

units.leftText: You shall dwell with us, and the land will be before you. Live and trade in it, and get possessions in it.”
units.rightText: You may settle among us, and the land will be open to you. Live here, move about freely, and acquire your own property.”

units.leftText: Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you will tell me I will give.
units.rightText: Then Shechem said to Dinah’s father and brothers, “Grant me this favor, and I will give you whatever you ask.

units.leftText: Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I will give whatever you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”
units.rightText: Demand a high dowry and an expensive gift, and I will give you whatever you ask. Only give me the girl as my wife!”

units.leftText: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit when they spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,
units.rightText: But because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah, Jacob’s sons answered him and his father Hamor deceitfully.

units.leftText: and said to them, “We can’t do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.
units.rightText: “We cannot do such a thing,” they said. “To give our sister to an uncircumcised man would be a disgrace to us.

units.leftText: Only on this condition will we consent to you. If you will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised,
units.rightText: We will consent to this on one condition, that you become circumcised like us — every one of your males.

units.leftText: then will we give our daughters to you; and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
units.rightText: Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We will dwell among you and become one people.

units.leftText: But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, then we will take our sister, and we will be gone.”
units.rightText: But if you will not agree to be circumcised, then we will take our sister and go.”

units.leftText: Their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.
units.rightText: Their offer seemed good to Hamor and his son Shechem.

units.leftText: The young man didn’t wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was honored above all the house of his father.
units.rightText: The young man, who was the most respected of all his father’s household, did not hesitate to fulfill this request, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter.

units.leftText: Hamor and Shechem, his son, came to the gate of their city, and talked with the men of their city, saying,
units.rightText: So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city and addressed the men of their city:

units.leftText: “These men are peaceful with us. Therefore let them live in the land and trade in it. For behold, the land is large enough for them. Let’s take their daughters to us for wives, and let’s give them our daughters.
units.rightText: “These men are at peace with us. Let them live and trade in our land; indeed, it is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters in marriage and give our daughters to them.

units.leftText: Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people, if every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.
units.rightText: But only on this condition will the men agree to dwell with us and be one people: if all our men are circumcised as they are.

units.leftText: Won’t their livestock and their possessions and all their animals be ours? Only let’s give our consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”
units.rightText: Will not their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals become ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell among us.”

units.leftText: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor, and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
units.rightText: All the men who went out of the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male of the city was circumcised.

units.leftText: On the third day, when they were sore, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the unsuspecting city, and killed all the males.
units.rightText: Three days later, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob’s sons (Dinah’s brothers Simeon and Levi) took their swords, went into the unsuspecting city, and slaughtered every male.

units.leftText: They killed Hamor and Shechem, his son, with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.
units.rightText: They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with their swords, took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.

units.leftText: Jacob’s sons came on the dead, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
units.rightText: Jacob’s other sons came upon the slaughter and looted the city, because their sister had been defiled.

units.leftText: They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, that which was in the city, that which was in the field,
units.rightText: They took their flocks and herds and donkeys, and everything else in the city or in the field.

units.leftText: and all their wealth. They took captive all their little ones and their wives, and took as plunder everything that was in the house.
units.rightText: They carried off all their possessions and women and children, and they plundered everything in their houses.

units.leftText: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number. They will gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house.”
units.rightText: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people of this land. We are few in number; if they unite against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed.”

units.leftText: They said, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”
units.rightText: But they replied, “Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?”

units.leftText: God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and live there. Make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.”
units.rightText: Then God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and settle there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.”

units.leftText: Then Jacob said to his household, and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your garments.
units.rightText: So Jacob told his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your garments.

units.leftText: Let’s arise, and go up to Bethel. I will make there an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me on the way which I went.”
units.rightText: Then let us arise and go to Bethel. I will build an altar there to God, who answered me in my day of distress. He has been with me wherever I have gone.”

units.leftText: They gave to Jacob all the foreign gods which were in their hands, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
units.rightText: So they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and all their earrings, and Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.
rightNotes: 35:4 Or terebinth or great tree

units.leftText: They traveled, and a terror of God was on the cities that were around them, and they didn’t pursue the sons of Jacob.
units.rightText: As they set out, a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities, so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.

units.leftText: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.
units.rightText: So Jacob and everyone with him arrived in Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: He built an altar there, and called the place El Beth El; because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
units.rightText: There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel, because it was there that God had revealed Himself to Jacob as he fled from his brother.
rightNotes: 35:7 El-bethel means God of Bethel.

units.leftText: Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was called Allon Bacuth.
units.rightText: Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. So Jacob named it Allon-bacuth.
rightNotes: 35:8 Or great tree
35:8 Allon-bacuth means oak of weeping.

units.leftText: God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.
units.rightText: After Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
rightNotes: 35:9 That is, northwest Mesopotamia; also in verse 26

units.leftText: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be Jacob any more, but your name will be Israel.” He named him Israel.
units.rightText: And God said to him, “Though your name is Jacob, you will no longer be called Jacob. Instead, your name will be Israel. ” So God named him Israel.
rightNotes: 35:10 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.
35:10 Israel means he struggles with God.

units.leftText: God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body.
units.rightText: And God told him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation — even a company of nations — shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.
rightNotes: 35:11 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”
units.rightText: The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you.”

units.leftText: God went up from him in the place where he spoke with him.
units.rightText: Then God went up from the place where He had spoken with him.

units.leftText: Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.
units.rightText: So Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him— a stone marker— and he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.

units.leftText: Jacob called the name of the place where God spoke with him “Bethel”.
units.rightText: Jacob called the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
rightNotes: 35:15 Bethel means house of God.

units.leftText: They traveled from Bethel. There was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.
units.rightText: Later, they set out from Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was difficult.

units.leftText: When she was in hard labor, the midwife said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for now you will have another son.”
units.rightText: During her severe labor, the midwife said to her, “Do not be afraid, for you are having another son.”

units.leftText: As her soul was departing (for she died), she named him Benoni, but his father named him Benjamin.
units.rightText: And with her last breath— for she was dying— she named vvv him Ben-oni. But his father called him Benjamin.
rightNotes: 35:18 Ben-oni could mean son of my sorrow or son of my strength.
35:18 Benjamin means son of my right hand.

units.leftText: Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath (also called Bethlehem).
units.rightText: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).

units.leftText: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave. The same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.
units.rightText: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave; it marks Rachel’s tomb to this day.

units.leftText: Israel traveled, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
units.rightText: Israel again set out and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder.

units.leftText: While Israel lived in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it.
units.rightText: While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard about it.

units.leftText: The sons of Leah: Reuben (Jacob’s firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
units.rightText: The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

units.leftText: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
units.rightText: The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.

units.leftText: The sons of Bilhah (Rachel’s servant): Dan and Naphtali.
units.rightText: The sons of Rachel’s maidservant Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali.

units.leftText: The sons of Zilpah (Leah’s servant): Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan Aram.
units.rightText: And the sons of Leah’s maidservant Zilpah were Gad and Asher.

units.leftText: Jacob came to Isaac his father, to Mamre, to Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac lived as foreigners.
units.rightText: Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.

units.leftText: The days of Isaac were one hundred eighty years.
units.rightText: And Isaac lived 180 years.

units.leftText: Isaac gave up the spirit and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.
units.rightText: Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

units.leftText: Now this is the history of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).
units.rightText: This is the account of Esau (that is, Edom).

units.leftText: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon, the Hittite; and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the Hivite;
units.rightText: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite,

units.leftText: and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.
units.rightText: and Basemath daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.

units.leftText: Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz. Basemath bore Reuel.
units.rightText: And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, Basemath gave birth to Reuel,

units.leftText: Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: and Oholibamah gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the members of his household, with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the land of Canaan, and went into a land away from his brother Jacob.
units.rightText: Later, Esau took his wives and sons and daughters and all the people of his household, along with his livestock, all his other animals, and all the property he had acquired in Canaan, and he moved to a land far away from his brother Jacob.

units.leftText: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their travels couldn’t bear them because of their livestock.
units.rightText: For their possessions were too great for them to dwell together; the land where they stayed could not support them because of their livestock.

units.leftText: Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.
units.rightText: So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir.

units.leftText: This is the history of the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir:
units.rightText: This is the account of Esau, the father of the Edomites, in the area of Mount Seir.

units.leftText: these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; and Reuel, the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
units.rightText: These are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz son of Esau’s wife Adah, and Reuel son of Esau’s wife Basemath.

units.leftText: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
units.rightText: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.

units.leftText: Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son; and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek. These are the descendants of Adah, Esau’s wife.
units.rightText: Additionally, Timna, a concubine of Esau’s son Eliphaz, gave birth to Amalek. These are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Adah.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the descendants of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. They are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.

units.leftText: These were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah (daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon) whom she bore to Esau: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

units.leftText: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
units.rightText: These are the chiefs among the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: Chiefs Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,

units.leftText: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs who came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Adah.
units.rightText: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. They are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom, and they are the grandsons of Adah.
rightNotes: 36:16 Hebrew; SP (also in verse 11 and 1 Chronicles 1:36|1CH 1:36*) does not include Korah.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs who came of Reuel in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Esau’s son Reuel: Chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. They are the chiefs descended from Reuel in the land of Edom, and they are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These are the chiefs who came of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah: Chiefs Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. They are the chiefs descended from Esau’s wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these are their chiefs.
units.rightText: All these are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and they were their chiefs.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
units.rightText: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who were living in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

units.leftText: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.
units.rightText: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. They are the chiefs of the Horites, the descendants of Seir in the land of Edom.

units.leftText: The children of Lotan were Hori and Heman. Lotan’s sister was Timna.
units.rightText: The sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam. Timna was Lotan’s sister.
rightNotes: 36:22 Hemam is a variant of Homam; see 1 Chronicles 1:39|1CH 1:39*.

units.leftText: These are the children of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

units.leftText: These are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Zibeon his father.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. (This is the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness as he was pasturing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.)

units.leftText: These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
units.rightText: These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.

units.leftText: These are the children of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
rightNotes: 36:26 Hebrew Dishan, a variant of Dishon

units.leftText: These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

units.leftText: These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

units.leftText: These are the chiefs who came of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
units.rightText: These are the chiefs of the Horites: Chiefs Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

units.leftText: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
units.rightText: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. They are the chiefs of the Horites, according to their divisions in the land of Seir.

units.leftText: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel.
units.rightText: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites:
rightNotes: 36:31 Or before an Israelite king reigned over them:

units.leftText: Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.
units.rightText: Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom; the name of his city was Dinhabah.

units.leftText: Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Husham died, and Hadad, the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith.
units.rightText: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Avith.

units.leftText: Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the Euphrates reigned in his place.
rightNotes: 36:37 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: Shaul died, and Baal Hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Baal Hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau. His wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
units.rightText: When Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, Hadad reigned in his place. His city was named Pau, and his wife’s name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
rightNotes: 36:39 Some MT manuscripts, SP, and Syriac (see also 1 Chronicles 1:50|1CH 1:50*); other MT manuscripts Hadar

units.leftText: These are the names of the chiefs who came from Esau, according to their families, after their places, and by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
units.rightText: These are the names of Esau’s chiefs, according to their families and regions, by their names: Chiefs Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

units.leftText: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
units.rightText: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

units.leftText: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
units.rightText: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

units.leftText: chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.
units.rightText: Magdiel, and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they possessed. Esau was the father of the Edomites.

units.leftText: Jacob lived in the land of his father’s travels, in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: Now Jacob lived in the land where his father had resided, the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: This is the history of the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers. He was a boy with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. Joseph brought an evil report of them to their father.
units.rightText: This is the account of Jacob. When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers, the sons of his father’s wives Bilhah and Zilpah, and he brought their father a bad report about them.

units.leftText: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a tunic of many colors.
units.rightText: Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.
rightNotes: 37:3 Possibly a robe with long sleeves; also in verses 23 and 32

units.leftText: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him, and couldn’t speak peaceably to him.
units.rightText: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.

units.leftText: Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him all the more.
units.rightText: Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Please hear this dream which I have dreamed:
units.rightText: He said to them, “Listen to this dream I had:

units.leftText: for behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves came around, and bowed down to my sheaf.”
units.rightText: We were binding sheaves of grain in the field, and suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.”

units.leftText: His brothers asked him, “Will you indeed reign over us? Will you indeed have dominion over us?” They hated him all the more for his dreams and for his words.
units.rightText: “Do you intend to reign over us?” his brothers asked. “Will you actually rule us?” So they hated him even more because of his dream and his statements.
