units.rightText: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted, thin and scorched by the east wind.

units.leftText: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
units.rightText: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven plump, ripe ones. Then Pharaoh awoke and realized it was a dream.

units.leftText: In the morning, his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt’s magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.
units.rightText: In the morning his spirit was troubled, so he summoned all the magicians and wise men of Egypt. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for him.

units.leftText: Then the chief cup bearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my faults today.
units.rightText: Then the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, “Today I recall my failures.

units.leftText: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, with the chief baker.
units.rightText: Pharaoh was once angry with his servants, and he put me and the chief baker in the custody of the captain of the guard.

units.leftText: We dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each man dreamed according to the interpretation of his dream.
units.rightText: One night both the chief baker and I had dreams, and each dream had its own meaning.

units.leftText: There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. He interpreted to each man according to his dream.
units.rightText: Now a young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams and he interpreted them for us individually.

units.leftText: As he interpreted to us, so it was. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”
units.rightText: And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged.”

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.
units.rightText: So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of the dungeon. After he had shaved and changed his clothes, he went in before Pharaoh.

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
units.rightText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”

units.leftText: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It isn’t in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
units.rightText: “I myself cannot do it,” Joseph replied, “but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.”

units.leftText: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river;
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph: “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile,

units.leftText: and behold, seven fat and sleek cattle came up out of the river. They fed in the marsh grass;
units.rightText: when seven cows, well-fed and sleek, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.

units.leftText: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
units.rightText: After them, seven other cows— sickly, ugly, and thin— came up. I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt!

units.leftText: The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle;
units.rightText: Then the thin, ugly cows devoured the seven well-fed cows that were there first.

units.leftText: and when they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
units.rightText: When they had devoured them, however, no one could tell that they had done so; their appearance was as ugly as it had been before. Then I awoke.

units.leftText: I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good;
units.rightText: In my dream I also saw seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, growing on a single stalk.

units.leftText: and behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.
units.rightText: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted— withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind.

units.leftText: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”
units.rightText: And the thin heads of grain swallowed the seven plump ones.

units.leftText: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.
units.rightText: At this, Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what He is about to do.

units.leftText: The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.
units.rightText: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven ripe heads of grain are seven years. The dreams have the same meaning.

units.leftText: The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; they will be seven years of famine.
units.rightText: Moreover, the seven thin, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven worthless heads of grain scorched by the east wind — they are seven years of famine.

units.leftText: That is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
units.rightText: It is just as I said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do.

units.leftText: Behold, seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt are coming.
units.rightText: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt,

units.leftText: Seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,
units.rightText: but seven years of famine will follow them. Then all the abundance in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will devastate the land.

units.leftText: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.
units.rightText: The abundance in the land will not be remembered, since the famine that follows it will be so severe.

units.leftText: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
units.rightText: Moreover, because the dream was given to Pharaoh in two versions, the matter has been decreed by God, and He will carry it out shortly.

units.leftText: “Now therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Now, therefore, Pharaoh should look for a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.
units.rightText: Let Pharaoh take action and appoint commissioners over the land to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
rightNotes: 41:34 See LXX; MT a fifth from the land

units.leftText: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and store grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
units.rightText: Under the authority of Pharaoh, let them collect all the excess food from these good years, that they may come and lay up the grain to be preserved as food in the cities.

units.leftText: The food will be to supply the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; so that the land will not perish through the famine.”
units.rightText: This food will be a reserve for the land during the seven years of famine to come upon the land of Egypt. Then the country will not perish in the famine.”

units.leftText: The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
units.rightText: This proposal pleased Pharaoh and all his officials.

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”
units.rightText: So Pharaoh asked them, “Can we find anyone like this man, in whom the Spirit of God abides?”
rightNotes: 41:38 Or the spirit of the gods

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Because God has shown you all of this, there is no one so discreet and wise as you.
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.

units.leftText: You shall be over my house. All my people will be ruled according to your word. Only in the throne I will be greater than you.”
units.rightText: You shall be in charge of my house, and all my people are to obey your commands. Only with regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
units.rightText: Pharaoh also told Joseph, “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.”

units.leftText: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger, clothed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a gold chain around his neck.

units.leftText: He made him ride in the second chariot which he had. They cried before him, “Bow the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: He had Joseph ride in his second chariot, with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!” So he placed him over all the land of Egypt.
rightNotes: 41:43 That is, “Abrek,” probably an Egyptian word that sounds similar to the Hebrew for kneel

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh. Without you, no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh declared to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.”

units.leftText: Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife. And Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt.
rightNotes: 41:45 Zaphenath-paneah probably means Revealer of Mysteries or God speaks and lives.
41:45 That is, Heliopolis, as in LXX; also in verse 50

units.leftText: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph left Pharaoh’s presence and traveled throughout the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.
units.rightText: During the seven years of abundance, the land brought forth bountifully.

units.leftText: He gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities. He stored food in each city from the fields around that city.
units.rightText: During those seven years, Joseph collected all the excess food in the land of Egypt and stored it in the cities. In every city he laid up the food from the fields around it.

units.leftText: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.
units.rightText: So Joseph stored up grain in such abundance, like the sand of the sea, that he stopped keeping track of it; for it was beyond measure.

units.leftText: To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
units.rightText: Before the years of famine arrived, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.

units.leftText: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”
units.rightText: Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, saying, “God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father’s household.”
rightNotes: 41:51 Manasseh sounds like the Hebrew for making to forget.

units.leftText: The name of the second, he called Ephraim: “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
units.rightText: And the second son he named Ephraim, saying, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
leftNotes: 41:52 “Ephraim” sounds like the Hebrew for “twice fruitful”.
rightNotes: 41:52 Ephraim sounds like the Hebrew for making fruitful or twice fruitful.

units.leftText: The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, came to an end.
units.rightText: When the seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt came to an end,

units.leftText: The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
units.rightText: the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. And although there was famine in every country, there was food throughout the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
units.rightText: When extreme hunger came to all the land of Egypt and the people cried out to Pharaoh for food, he told all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.”

units.leftText: The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: When the famine had spread over all the land, Joseph opened up all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians; for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
units.rightText: And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.

units.leftText: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”
units.rightText: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you staring at one another?”

units.leftText: He said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”
units.rightText: “Look,” he added, “I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.”

units.leftText: Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
units.rightText: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

units.leftText: But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he said, “Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”
units.rightText: But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers, for he said, “I am afraid that harm might befall him.”

units.leftText: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: So the sons of Israel were among those who came to buy grain, since the famine had also spread to the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.
units.rightText: Now Joseph was the ruler of the land; he was the one who sold grain to all its people. So when his brothers arrived, they bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.

units.leftText: Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?”
units.rightText: And when Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he treated them as strangers and spoke harshly to them. “Where have you come from?” he asked.

units.leftText: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.
units.rightText: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.

units.leftText: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
units.rightText: Joseph remembered his dreams about them and said, “You are spies! You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.”

units.leftText: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
units.rightText: “Not so, my lord,” they replied. “Your servants have come to buy food.

units.leftText: We are all one man’s sons; we are honest men. Your servants are not spies.”
units.rightText: We are all sons of one man. Your servants are honest men, not spies.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”
units.rightText: “No,” he told them. “You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.”

units.leftText: They said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is today with our father, and one is no more.”
units.rightText: But they answered, “Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.”

units.leftText: Joseph said to them, “It is like I told you, saying, ‘You are spies!’
units.rightText: Then Joseph declared, “Just as I said, you are spies!

units.leftText: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.
units.rightText: And this is how you will be tested: As surely as Pharaoh lives, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.

units.leftText: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.”
units.rightText: Send one of your number to get your brother; the rest of you will be confined so that the truth of your words may be tested. If they are untrue, then as surely as Pharaoh lives, you are spies!”

units.leftText: He put them all together into custody for three days.
units.rightText: So Joseph imprisoned them for three days,

units.leftText: Joseph said to them the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.
units.rightText: and on the third day he said to them, “I fear God. So do this and you will live:

units.leftText: If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.
units.rightText: If you are honest, leave one of your brothers in custody while the rest of you go and take back grain to relieve the hunger of your households.

units.leftText: Bring your youngest brother to me; so will your words be verified, and you won’t die.”
units.rightText: Then bring your youngest brother to me so that your words can be verified, that you may not die.”

units.leftText: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”
units.rightText: Then they said to one another, “Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us.”

units.leftText: Reuben answered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘Don’t sin against the child,’ and you wouldn’t listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.”
units.rightText: And Reuben responded, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen. Now we must account for his blood!”

units.leftText: They didn’t know that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.
units.rightText: They did not realize that Joseph understood them, since there was an interpreter between them.

units.leftText: He turned himself away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
units.rightText: And he turned away from them and wept. When he turned back and spoke to them, he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.

units.leftText: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.
units.rightText: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to return each man’s silver to his sack, and to give them provisions for their journey. This order was carried out,
rightNotes: 42:25 Or money; here and throughout chapters 42–44

units.leftText: They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.
units.rightText: and they loaded the grain on their donkeys and departed.

units.leftText: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
units.rightText: At the place where they lodged for the night, one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of the sack.

units.leftText: He said to his brothers, “My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!” Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”
units.rightText: “My silver has been returned!” he said to his brothers. “It is here in my sack.”

units.leftText: They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,
units.rightText: When they reached their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they described to him all that had happened to them:

units.leftText: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.
units.rightText: “The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly to us and accused us of spying on the country.

units.leftText: We said to him, ‘We are honest men. We are no spies.
units.rightText: But we told him, ‘We are honest men, not spies.

units.leftText: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Canaan.’
units.rightText: We are twelve brothers, sons of one father. One is no more, and the youngest is now with our father in the land of Canaan.’

units.leftText: The man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way.
units.rightText: Then the man who is lord of the land said to us, ‘This is how I will know whether you are honest: Leave one brother with me, take food to relieve the hunger of your households, and go.

units.leftText: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”
units.rightText: But bring your youngest brother back to me so I will know that you are not spies but honest men. Then I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in the land.’”

units.leftText: As they emptied their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.
units.rightText: As they began emptying their sacks, there in each man’s sack was his bag of silver! And when they and their father saw the bags of silver, they were dismayed.

units.leftText: Jacob, their father, said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.”
units.rightText: Their father Jacob said to them, “You have deprived me of my sons. Joseph is gone and Simeon is no more. Now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is going against me!”

units.leftText: Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “Kill my two sons, if I don’t bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him to you again.”
units.rightText: Then Reuben said to his father, “You may kill my two sons if I fail to bring him back to you. Put him in my care, and I will return him.”

units.leftText: He said, “My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.”
units.rightText: But Jacob replied, “My son will not go down there with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If any harm comes to him on your journey, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.”
leftNotes: 42:38 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: The famine was severe in the land.
units.rightText: Now the famine was still severe in the land.

units.leftText: When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”
units.rightText: So when Jacob’s sons had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”

units.leftText: Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’
units.rightText: But Judah replied, “The man solemnly warned us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’

units.leftText: If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food;
units.rightText: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.

units.leftText: but if you don’t send him, we won’t go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’”
units.rightText: But if you will not send him, we will not go; for the man told us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’”

units.leftText: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”
units.rightText: “Why did you bring this trouble upon me?” Israel asked. “Why did you tell the man you had another brother?”

units.leftText: They said, “The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”
units.rightText: They replied, “The man questioned us in detail about ourselves and our family: ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ And we answered him accordingly. How could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother here’?”

units.leftText: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.
units.rightText: And Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the boy with me, and we will go at once, so that we may live and not die— neither we, nor you, nor our children.

units.leftText: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;
units.rightText: I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible. If I do not bring him back and set him before you, then may I bear the guilt before you all my life.

units.leftText: for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now.”
units.rightText: If we had not delayed, we could have come and gone twice by now.”

units.leftText: Their father, Israel, said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
units.rightText: Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your packs and carry them down as a gift for the man — a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.

units.leftText: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.
units.rightText: Take double the silver with you so that you may return the silver that was put back into the mouths of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.

units.leftText: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.
units.rightText: Take your brother as well, and return to the man at once.

units.leftText: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”
units.rightText: May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release your other brother along with Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”
rightNotes: 43:14 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
units.rightText: So the men took these gifts, along with double the amount of silver, and Benjamin as well. Then they hurried down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

units.leftText: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”
units.rightText: When Joseph saw Benjamin with his brothers, he said to the steward of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they shall dine with me at noon.”

units.leftText: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.
units.rightText: The man did as Joseph had commanded and took the brothers to Joseph’s house.

units.leftText: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
units.rightText: But the brothers were frightened that they had been taken to Joseph’s house. “We have been brought here because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time,” they said. “They intend to overpower us and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”

units.leftText: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,
units.rightText: So they approached Joseph’s steward and spoke to him at the entrance to the house.

units.leftText: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.
units.rightText: “Please, sir,” they said, “we really did come down here the first time to buy food.

units.leftText: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.
units.rightText: But when we came to the place we lodged for the night, we opened our sacks and, behold, each of us found his silver in the mouth of his sack! It was the full amount of our silver, and we have brought it back with us.

units.leftText: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”
units.rightText: We have brought additional silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”

units.leftText: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.
units.rightText: “It is fine,” said the steward. “Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, gave you the treasure that was in your sacks. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.

units.leftText: The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.
units.rightText: And the steward took the men into Joseph’s house, gave them water to wash their feet, and provided food for their donkeys.

units.leftText: They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.
units.rightText: Since the brothers had been told that they were going to eat a meal there, they prepared their gift for Joseph’s arrival at noon.

units.leftText: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to the earth before him.
units.rightText: When Joseph came home, they presented him with the gifts they had brought, and they bowed to the ground before him.

units.leftText: He asked them of their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”
units.rightText: He asked if they were well, and then he asked, “How is your elderly father you told me about? Is he still alive?”

units.leftText: They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.
units.rightText: “Your servant our father is well,” they answered. “He is still alive.” And they bowed down to honor him.

units.leftText: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
units.rightText: When Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother’s son, he asked, “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” Then he declared, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”

units.leftText: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
units.rightText: Joseph hurried out because he was moved to tears for his brother, and he went to a private room to weep.

units.leftText: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”
units.rightText: Then he washed his face and came back out. Regaining his composure, he said, “Serve the meal.”

units.leftText: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
units.rightText: They separately served Joseph, his brothers, and the Egyptians. They ate separately because the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them.

units.leftText: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled with one another.
units.rightText: They were seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn to the youngest, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.

units.leftText: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.
units.rightText: When the portions were served to them from Joseph’s table, Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of the others. So they feasted and drank freely with Joseph.

units.leftText: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
units.rightText: Then Joseph instructed his steward: “Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each one’s silver in the mouth of his sack.

units.leftText: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
units.rightText: Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack, along with the silver for his grain.”

units.leftText: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
units.rightText: At daybreak, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.

units.leftText: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?
units.rightText: They had not gone far from the city when Joseph told his steward, “Pursue the men at once, and when you overtake them, ask, ‘Why have you repaid good with evil?
rightNotes: 44:4 LXX includes Why have you stolen my silver cup?

units.leftText: Isn’t this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”
units.rightText: Is this not the cup my master drinks from and uses for divination? What you have done is wicked!’”
rightNotes: 44:5 Hebrew Is it not this which

units.leftText: He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.
units.rightText: When the steward overtook them, he relayed these words to them.

units.leftText: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!
units.rightText: “Why does my lord say these things?” they asked. “Your servants could not possibly do such a thing.

units.leftText: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?
units.rightText: We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found in the mouths of our sacks. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?

units.leftText: With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”
units.rightText: If any of your servants is found to have it, he must die, and the rest will become slaves of my lord.”

units.leftText: He said, “Now also let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found will be my slave; and you will be blameless.”
units.rightText: “As you say,” replied the steward. “But only the one who is found with the cup will be my slave, and the rest of you shall be free of blame.”

units.leftText: Then they hurried, and each man took his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
units.rightText: So each one quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it.

units.leftText: He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
units.rightText: The steward searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest — and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

units.leftText: Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.
units.rightText: Then they all tore their clothes, loaded their donkeys, and returned to the city.

units.leftText: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.
units.rightText: When Judah and his brothers arrived at Joseph’s house, he was still there, and they fell to the ground before him.

units.leftText: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”
units.rightText: “What is this deed you have done?” Joseph declared. “Do you not know that a man like me can surely divine the truth?”

units.leftText: Judah said, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? How will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup is found.”
units.rightText: “What can we say to my lord?” Judah replied. “How can we plead? How can we justify ourselves? God has exposed the iniquity of your servants. We are now my lord’s slaves— both we and the one who was found with the cup.”

units.leftText: He said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
units.rightText: But Joseph replied, “Far be it from me to do this. The man who was found with the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may return to your father in peace.”

units.leftText: Then Judah came near to him, and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.
units.rightText: Then Judah approached Joseph and said, “Sir, please let your servant speak personally to my lord. Do not be angry with your servant, for you are equal to Pharaoh himself.

units.leftText: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’
units.rightText: My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’

units.leftText: We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
units.rightText: And we answered, ‘We have an elderly father and a younger brother, the child of his old age. The boy’s brother is dead. He is the only one of his mother’s sons left, and his father loves him.’

units.leftText: You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
units.rightText: Then you told your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so that I can see him for myself.’

units.leftText: We said to my lord, ‘The boy can’t leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
units.rightText: So we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he were to leave, his father would die.’

units.leftText: You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.’
units.rightText: But you said to your servants, ‘Unless your younger brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’

units.leftText: When we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
units.rightText: Now when we returned to your servant my father, we relayed your words to him.

units.leftText: Our father said, ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’
units.rightText: Then our father said, ‘Go back and buy us some food.’

units.leftText: We said, ‘We can’t go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down: for we may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is with us.’
units.rightText: But we answered, ‘We cannot go down there unless our younger brother goes with us. So if our younger brother is not with us, we cannot see the man.’

units.leftText: Your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
units.rightText: And your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.

units.leftText: One went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn in pieces;” and I haven’t seen him since.
units.rightText: When one of them was gone, I said: “Surely he has been torn to pieces.” And I have not seen him since.

units.leftText: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’
units.rightText: Now if you also take this one from me and harm comes to him, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.’
leftNotes: 44:29 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;
units.rightText: So if the boy is not with us when I return to your servant, and if my father, whose life is wrapped up in the boy’s life,

units.leftText: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.
units.rightText: sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. Then your servants will have brought the gray hair of your servant our father down to Sheol in sorrow.
leftNotes: 44:31 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’
units.rightText: Indeed, your servant guaranteed the boy’s safety to my father, saying, ‘If I do not return him to you, I will bear the guilt before you, my father, all my life.’

units.leftText: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.
units.rightText: Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy. Let him return with his brothers.

units.leftText: For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t with me?—lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”
units.rightText: For how can I go back to my father without the boy? I could not bear to see the misery that would overwhelm him.”

units.leftText: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
units.rightText: Then Joseph could no longer control himself before all his attendants, and he cried out, “Send everyone away from me!”

units.leftText: He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
units.rightText: But he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh’s household soon heard of it.

units.leftText: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Does my father still live?”
units.rightText: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?”

units.leftText: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.”
units.rightText: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Please come near me.” And they did so.

units.leftText: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
units.rightText: And now, do not be distressed or angry with yourselves that you sold me into this place, because it was to save lives that God sent me before you.

units.leftText: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.
units.rightText: For the famine has covered the land these two years, and there will be five more years without plowing or harvesting.

units.leftText: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
units.rightText: God sent me before you to preserve you as a remnant on the earth and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
rightNotes: 45:7 Or and to keep you alive as a great band of survivors

units.leftText: So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God, who has made me a father to Pharaoh — lord of all his household and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t wait.
units.rightText: Now return quickly to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me without delay.

units.leftText: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
units.rightText: You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me— you and your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you own.

units.leftText: There I will provide for you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.”’
units.rightText: And there I will provide for you, because there will be five more years of famine. Otherwise, you and your household and everything you own will come to destitution.’

units.leftText: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
units.rightText: Behold! You and my brother Benjamin can see that I, Joseph, am the one speaking with you.

units.leftText: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”
units.rightText: Tell my father about all my splendor in Egypt and everything you have seen. And bring my father down here quickly.”

units.leftText: He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
units.rightText: Then Joseph threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept as they embraced.

units.leftText: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.
units.rightText: Joseph kissed each of his brothers as he wept over them. And afterward his brothers talked with him.

units.leftText: The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
units.rightText: When the news reached Pharaoh’s house that Joseph’s brothers had come, Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do as follows: Load your animals and return to the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’
units.rightText: Then bring your father and your families and return to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat from the fat of the land.’

units.leftText: Now you are commanded to do this: Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
units.rightText: You are also directed to tell them: ‘Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your young children and your wives, and bring your father and come back.

units.leftText: Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”
units.rightText: But pay no regard to your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’”

units.leftText: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
units.rightText: So the sons of Israel did as they were told. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had instructed, and he also gave them provisions for their journey.

units.leftText: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
units.rightText: He gave new garments to each of them, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes.
rightNotes: 45:22 300 shekels is approximately 7.5 pounds or 3.4 kilograms of silver.

units.leftText: He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.
units.rightText: And he sent to his father the following: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provisions for his father’s journey.

units.leftText: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”
units.rightText: Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way, and as they were leaving, he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way!”

units.leftText: They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
units.rightText: So the brothers went up out of Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.
units.rightText: “Joseph is still alive,” they said, “and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!”

units.leftText: They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.
units.rightText: However, when they relayed all that Joseph had told them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob was revived.

units.leftText: Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”
units.rightText: “Enough!” declared Israel. “My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die.”

units.leftText: Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.
units.rightText: So Israel set out with all that he had, and when he came to Beersheba, he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.

units.leftText: God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “Jacob, Jacob!”
units.rightText: And that night God spoke to Israel in a vision: “Jacob, Jacob!” He said.

units.leftText: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation.
units.rightText: “I am God,” He said, “the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.

units.leftText: I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”
units.rightText: I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back. And Joseph’s own hands will close your eyes.”

units.leftText: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
units.rightText: Then Jacob departed from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel took their father Jacob in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him, along with their children and wives.

units.leftText: They took their livestock, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt—Jacob, and all his offspring with him,
units.rightText: They also took the livestock and possessions they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and Jacob and all his offspring went to Egypt.

units.leftText: his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he brought all his offspring with him into Egypt.
units.rightText: Jacob took with him to Egypt his sons and grandsons, and his daughters and granddaughters — all his offspring.

units.leftText: These are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
units.rightText: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel (Jacob and his descendants) who went to Egypt: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.

units.leftText: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
units.rightText: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

units.leftText: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
units.rightText: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
rightNotes: 46:10 Jemuel is another name for Nemuel; see Numbers 26:12|NUM 26:12*.
46:10 Zohar is a variant of Zerah; see Numbers 26:13|NUM 26:13* and 1 Chronicles 4:24.

units.leftText: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
units.rightText: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

units.leftText: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
units.rightText: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
units.rightText: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Job, and Shimron.
rightNotes: 46:13 Hebrew; SP and Syriac Puah; see 1 Chronicles 7:1|1CH 7:1*.
46:13 Hebrew; SP and some LXX manuscripts Jashub; see Numbers 26:24|NUM 26:24* and 1 Chronicles 7:1.

units.leftText: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
units.rightText: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Leah born to Jacob in Paddan-aram, in addition to his daughter Dinah. The total number of sons and daughters was thirty-three.
rightNotes: 46:15 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
units.rightText: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
rightNotes: 46:16 SP and LXX Zephon; see also Numbers 26:15|NUM 26:15*.
46:16 Arodi is a variant of Arod; see Numbers 26:17|NUM 26:17*.

units.leftText: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
units.rightText: The children of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Jacob born to Zilpah — whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah — sixteen in all.

units.leftText: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
units.rightText: The sons of Jacob’s wife Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

units.leftText: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
units.rightText: Manasseh and Ephraim were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
rightNotes: 46:20 That is, Heliopolis, as in LXX

units.leftText: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
units.rightText: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Rachel born to Jacob — fourteen in all.

units.leftText: The son of Dan: Hushim.
units.rightText: The son of Dan: Hushim.

units.leftText: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
units.rightText: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Jacob born to Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel — seven in all.

units.leftText: All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct offspring, in addition to Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were sixty-six.
units.rightText: All those belonging to Jacob who came to Egypt— his direct descendants, besides the wives of Jacob’s sons— numbered sixty-six persons.

units.leftText: The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy.
units.rightText: And with the two sons who had been born to Joseph in Egypt, the members of Jacob’s family who went to Egypt were seventy in all.
rightNotes: 46:27 Hebrew; LXX the nine sons, probably including Joseph’s grandsons through Ephraim and Manasseh; see 1 Chronicles 7:14–29|1CH 7:14-29*.

units.leftText: Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.

units.leftText: Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.

units.leftText: When that year was ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, “We will not hide from my lord how our money is all spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord’s. There is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.

units.leftText: Joseph lived in Egypt, he, and his father’s house. Joseph lived one hundred ten years.
units.rightText: Now Joseph and his father’s household remained in Egypt, and Joseph lived to the age of 110.

units.leftText: Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.
units.rightText: He saw Ephraim’s sons to the third generation, and indeed the sons of Machir son of Manasseh were brought up on Joseph’s knees.
rightNotes: 50:23 Or born or placed at birth

units.leftText: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
units.rightText: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land He promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”

units.leftText: Joseph took an oath from the children of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”
units.rightText: And Joseph made the sons of Israel take an oath and said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.”

units.leftText: So Joseph died, being one hundred ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
units.rightText: So Joseph died at the age of 110. And they embalmed his body and placed it in a coffin in Egypt.
